News.title: Six arrested after man stabbed & rushed to hospital with ‘serious injuries to head and hand’
News.content:
STABBING PROBE Six arrested after man stabbed & rushed to hospital with ‘serious injuries to head and hand’

COPS have arrested six men after a man was reportedly stabbed in the street.

A 19-year-old man was found by police on London Road in Portsmouth just after 8pm on July 30.

He suffered “serious, but not life-threatening” injuries to his head and hand, according to officers.



The teenager was taken to hospital for treatment.



An investigation was launched which resulted in six people being arrested.

A 20-year-old man from Croydon was arrested on suspicion of wounding with intent; an 18-year-old man from Birmingham was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent, and a 24-year-old man from Birmingham was arrested on suspicion of wounding with intent and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place.

A police spokesperson said: “They remain in police custody at this time and enquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances.”



As the investigation progressed, three more men were arrested.

A 23-year-old man from Birmingham was arrested on suspicion of wounding with intent and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place; a 17-year-old boy from Birmingham was arrested on suspicion of wounding with intent and a 17-year-old boy from Wolverhampton was arrested on suspicion of assault, wounding with intent and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place.

They have now been released from custody and will face no further action in relation to these arrests.

News.title: At least three dead & 5 injured after ‘gunman opens fire’ outside In-N-Out as cops hunt for ‘shooter still at large’
News.content:
THREE people have been killed after at least one gunman opened fire at an In-N-Out burger chain in Idaho – sparking a major manhunt.

A rifle-wielding suspect began shooting at victims in the drive-thru area of the restaurant.



Terrified bystanders were seen running for their lives across the car park as the suspect fired a large AR-style assault weapon.

Another possible shooter was seen firing a handgun, but it was not clear if they were a secondary gunman or a responding witness.



Idaho Falls city spokesperson Josh Palmer told NBC News that at least three people had lost their lives and five others were injured.

He could not confirm whether the shooter was among the deceased.

Bullets began ringing out at around 3pm local time, with shocking footage showing dozens of people fleeing for their lives.

The suspect drove up to the chain’s drive-thru before exiting a white vehicle and retrieving a rifle from his trunk.



The man, wearing a black T-shirt and blue trousers, was seen walking through the car park before shooting through a Tesla‘s windscreen.

Twin Falls police confirmed they are responding to an active shooter situation near the In-N-Out.

Officers have been scouring a hotel that overlooks the complex where the shooting broke out.

They said that they would be enforcing a lockdown and closing multiple roads and bridges while they search for the suspect, urging people to avoid the area.

Idaho Governor Brad Little wrote on X: “Idahoans, join me in keeping the Twin Falls community in your prayers as law enforcement and first responders respond to an active shooter situation near In-N-Out.



“Please avoid the area and follow directions from law enforcement as they work to keep everyone safe.”

Attorney General Raul Labrador confirmed that cops were still searching for the suspect.

He said: “Praying for everyone in Twin Falls as first responders continue searching for the suspect near In-N-Out.

“Twin Falls Police, Idaho State Police, and fire and paramedic crews remain on scene working to secure the area.

“If you’re in the area, please listen to local authorities and stay away from In-N-Out and the surrounding streets so first responders can do their jobs.”



The FBI confirmed it would be assisting in the investigation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Authorities are yet to publicly identify the shooter or shooters, as well as a possible motive.

The investigation remains ongoing.

News.title: Two bikers rushed to hospital with serious injuries after horrific crash as air ambulance called to scene
News.content:
MOTORBIKE HORROR Two bikers rushed to hospital with serious injuries after horrific crash as air ambulance called to scene

TWO bikers were rushed to hospital after a major collision, with the air ambulance called to the scene.

The incident took place near Glossop on the A57 Snake Pass – one of the highest roads in the Peak District – on 4pm on Saturday.



Emergency services were called to the site and part of the road was cordoned off.

One rider in his 20s sustained severe injuries, which were not believed to be life-threatening.



The other rider was a man in his 70s, who escaped the crash without suffering serious injuries.

A spokesperson for Derbyshire Police said: “We were called to a report of a collision between two motorbikes on the A57 Snakes Pass close to Glossop just after 4pm today.



“Both riders were taken to hospital for treatment.

“A man in his 20s is understood to have sustained serious, but not life-threatening injuries, and a man in his 70s is not believed to be seriously hurt.”

News.title: Mother ‘scrolled on porn sites and watched TikToks’ as her six-month-old son was dying, cops say
News.content:
SICK 'NEGLECT' Mother ‘scrolled on porn sites and watched TikToks’ as her six-month-old son was dying, cops say

A MOTHER allegedly scrolled through TikTok and visited pornographic websites more than 30 times as her six-month-old son was dying, police say.

Tatiana Norman is accused of deliberately throwing little Jeremiah Peters into a playpen before failing to get him medical help as his condition deteriorated.



The tragic baby was eventually found unresponsive at Norman’s home on West Chestnut Drive in Lakeland, Florida, shortly before midnight on June 29.

Jeremiah was rushed to Lakeland Regional Hospital but was pronounced dead at 12.32am on June 30.



Police Chief Sammy Taylor Jr said the child may already have been dead for hours before his mum finally called 911.

Taylor said: “I think the child was probably deceased hours before she called us, just based on the evidence and the temperature of the body and the temperature a child should be.



“I think the child’s temperature when he got to the emergency room was 94, so I feel like he’d been dead for several hours by the time she decided to call us.”

Norman initially told cops she had put Jeremiah to bed while she prepared a bottle, only to return and find him lying on the tiled floor after falling from the bed.

But detectives say she later changed her story, claiming she had been sleeping beside Jeremiah and her one-year-old when they may have rolled onto the baby.

An autopsy allegedly tore apart her accounts, finding injuries that did not match her explanations.



The examination also found an unexplained mark on Jeremiah’s thigh was not caused by hot bathwater, as Norman had claimed, but by “a more significant thermal event.”

Police say Norman eventually confessed to a series of shocking incidents on the day her son died.

According to an arrest affidavit, she told detectives that at around 9am she accidentally dropped Jeremiah face-first while reaching for a remote.

Rather than seeking urgent medical help, she allegedly searched online for concussion symptoms and monitored him at home.

Jeremiah then allegedly suffered another brutal fall when Norman’s one-year-old climbed into his rocking bassinet, causing it to topple over.



Police say the infant again landed face-first.

Norman also allegedly gave detectives a string of conflicting explanations for the burn on Jeremiah’s leg.

She initially blamed laundry detergent used by the baby’s father before admitting she had spilled microwave noodle broth onto his leg, according to the affidavit.

The document stated: “Norman advised she contacted Jeremiah’s pediatrician via telephone regarding that injury.

“It should be noted that the injury to Jeremiah’s leg is not consistent with any of the statements provided to law enforcement.”



Then, at around 1pm, police say Norman became overwhelmed by her crying children.

Detectives allege she “intentionally ‘tossed’ or ‘threw’ Jeremiah into a playpen from a standing position” from several feet away.

During her explanation, Norman reportedly demonstrated both an underhand and an overhand throw.

Police say Jeremiah slammed his back and head into the playpen, which had no cushion on its base.

Norman allegedly told detectives that her son did not cry after the impact.



Taylor said: “When she threw the infant into the playpen, a visceral and obvious reaction of curling his hands and pulling his hands up, I think that’s probably when the significant injury occurred.”

Jeremiah then allegedly became increasingly lethargic and drank less formula, but police say Norman still did not seek medical attention.

Her phone activity has now emerged as a chilling part of the investigation.

At 2.10pm, Norman allegedly searched Google for “baby feels cold”, followed minutes later by “what happens when baby had concussion in Florida”.

Yet police say she then switched to TikTok, watching two videos including a cooking clip at 3.34pm.



The affidavit states she returned to the cooking video repeatedly until 4.23pm.

Even more disturbingly, detectives say Norman accessed pornographic websites more than 30 times while Jeremiah’s condition continued to worsen.

The baby’s father later texted Norman at around 10pm asking for a photograph of his son, but allegedly received no response before discovering Jeremiah was no longer breathing.

The Polk County Medical Examiner’s Office said Jeremiah might have survived if he had received medical attention immediately, according to the affidavit.

The affidavit states she described feeling depressed and having suicidal thoughts, as well as a history of PTSD and borderline personality disorder.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Norman has been charged with one count of aggravated child abuse.

The charges could be upgraded as prosecutors continue their investigation.

News.title: Britain must kick out overseas criminals or slash foreign aid until their countries take them back
News.content:
Kick out overseas crims, or slash aid

LAW-ABIDING Brits are sick of seeing vicious crooks walk away from prison less than halfway through their sentences.

It is a disgrace that prison overcrowding has led to Labour’s open door policy for thousands of villains who will never serve their terms in full.



Andy Burnham has slammed the brakes on the scheme after the outrage over the potential early release of the two killers of PC Andrew Harper.

But it is a scramble against the clock. Around 6,000 lags were due to go free from September 2 under the plan.



Without that, prison bosses warn jails will start running out of space in November.

So since every cell place counts, why are we still hosting more than 10,000 foreign prisoners?

It is insane that thousands who should be serving time in their own country’s jails are taking up scarce places in our own.

Successive governments have failed to cut numbers of overseas inmates.

The row over deporting grooming gang leader Shabir Ahmed to Pakistan shows how unsuccessful we have been. But there is a bargaining chip we could use.

Two countries with large groups of their nationals in our prisons are India and Albania.



The former receives nearly £25million in foreign aid and the latter got £4million in 2025.

Neither should receive a penny in aid again until they take back their citizens from our crisis-hit jails.

Regulate funerals

ONE thing is clear from the trial of funeral home monster Robert Bush.

The Wild West culture surrounding this business must end for good.

Hundreds of mourning relatives had their lives ruined by the evil of one man.



But the freedom he enjoyed to hoodwink victims under a cloak of secrecy while siphoning off their cash can and should be stopped immediately.

The Government must step in and regulate the funeral business without delay.

Bush had a parlour and chapel under the same roof. Such madness can’t go on.

It gives twisted individuals a licence to act with impunity.

It’s full-time, Gianni

“A SHABBY, backroom, opaque deal.’’



We couldn’t agree more with Uefa’s assessment of Gianni Infantino’s shameful collapsed plan to sell the World Cup.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

With every day that passes the Fifa chief’s position gets weaker.

It’s time to blow the final whistle… with no extra-time.

News.title: Fugitive accused over Athens firebomb deaths worked at Gatwick duty free for six years
News.content:
GATWICK FUGITIVE Fugitive accused over Athens firebomb deaths worked at Gatwick duty free for six years

A FUGITIVE accused of being part of a fatal firebombing has been working at a Gatwick airport duty free shop for years.

Eleni Argyriou, 46, was arrested last month in connection with the attack on a bank in Athens in 2010 in which three people died.



She was held by officers from the National Extradition Unit at Gatwick as she was about to board a flight to her native Greece.

Argyriou is thought to have been living in Sussex for seven years.



According to her LinkedIn page, she has worked as a sales assistant at the World Duty Free Shop at Gatwick since April 2019.

Avolta, which operates the duty free business, and the airport declined to comment.

The day after her arrest she appeared at Westminster magistrates’ court and consented to her deportation.

Argyriou is now in custody and is due to be flown back by August 14.

She faces trial in Athens for three murders and domestic extremism.

Masked anarchists threw petrol bombs into the Marfin Bank, setting it ablaze, as tens of thousands protested during the Greek financial crisis in May 2010.



Around 30 workers were inside.

Most managed to flee but three clerks, including a pregnant lady, were trapped and died from asphyxia.

Greek prosecutors believe Argyriou was part of an anarchy group responsible.

Two 42-year-old men were arrested in Athens last month and are in custody awaiting trial.

Police are still trying to identify other suspects.



According to reports in Greece, the arrests followed the publication of a 117-page forensic report that provided evidence, including ­photos and videos, that helped to identify suspects.

It is also claimed that an anonymous email was sent to Greece’s organised crime squad naming Argyriou and the two men arrested.

She has previously said she would voluntarily return to prove her innocence.

The Crown Prosecution Service said Argyriou was accused by Greek authorities of “operational planning, joint action, and with a shared homicidal intent — thereby killing three individuals”.

News.title: ‘Flying saucer’ shock at Gatwick as mystery disc whizzes past passenger jet during landing
News.content:
THE pilot of a passenger jet reported seeing a “flying saucer” feet away from the aircraft as it came in to land.

And the crew of another plane told investigators a drone had come so close they could make out markings and see its propellers.



The flying saucer incident occurred in April as the Airbus prepared to touch down at Gatwick.

A report by investigators at the UK Airprox Board revealed the following.



“The A319 pilot reports that descending, turning left, a disc or ‘flying saucer’ type ­suspected drone was seen flying very close in the opposite direction, at the same level to them, past their right wing.

“Approximately 100-300ft from their aircraft wing. The object looked like a disc with darker markings on the rim, a suspected possible drone but not sure.



“It was very close to the aircraft, but no ­evasive action was required as they were in a turn already.”

The board ruled that the safety of the aircraft had been “reduced”.

A second drone ­incident also occurred in April at London’s Heathrow airport.

The board revealed: “The A321 pilot reports that, whilst in a left turn on to base leg at LHR (over Marlow), a drone was witnessed to fly down the left-hand-side of the aircraft at close enough proximity to see details such as the colour, shape and individual props spinning.”



Airprox officials ruled: “The board considered that providence had played a major part in the incident and/or a definite risk of collision had existed.”

Last week the UK Airprox Board revealed that two RAF pilots had seen a possible UFO during an air-to-air refuelling over the North Sea near Norfolk in February.

One in the Voyager tanker ducked as the object whizzed past between 100ft and 150ft away at 16,000ft.

The pilot in the Typhoon fighter being refuelled also saw the object but it did not appear on radar.

News.title: Burnham facing first rebellion over North Sea drilling as green light sparks Labour revolt
News.content:
NORTH Sea drilling is expected to be approved within weeks — setting up Andy Burnham’s first Labour rebellion.

The new PM has told US President Donald Trump that he will take a “pragmatic” approach to oil and gas exploration.



Jackdaw — a major gas project operated by Shell — is expected to be given the green light towards the end of summer, The Sun on Sunday understands.

This would be a much-needed boost for jobs and growth in the industry after BP announced plans to sell its UK North Sea oil and gas business.



But lefties in Mr Burnham’s party are already gearing up to kick off at the announcement, in what looks set to be the first major row of his premiership.

Labour MP Clive Lewis said there was “no legitimate reason” to push ahead with the drilling.



Another, Rachael Maskell, also hit out at the proposals.

But Scottish Labour MPs have been privately urging Mr ­Burnham to allow new drilling in the North Sea, to create jobs and revenue for the area.

One Scottish Labour MP said: “We have all been telling him the same thing — we need to get drilling.”

The decision on drilling at Jackdaw and the Rosebank site lies with the Energy Security and Net Zero Secretary.



When he was in the job, Ed Miliband was widely seen as blocking the approval.

But he is Foreign Secretary now and his replacement Miatta Fahnbulleh is serving as a strong ally of Mr Burnham, who is keen to show he is a pro-jobs PM.

A spokesman for the Net Zero department said they cannot comment on individual projects.

News.title: Donald Trump hints at new Iran deal that could end war - 'US is locked and loaded'
News.content:
Donald Trump hints at new Iran deal that could end war - 'US is locked and loaded'

It comes as the Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the kingdom’s de facto leader, expressed in a phone call with Trump his concerns about the US potentially escalating the conflict with Iran

View 3 Images Donald Trump has posted an update on Truth Social (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump has claimed that Mideast allies have reached the parameters of a deal to end the Iran war while warning that the United States remains 'locked and loaded' and ready to launch an attack.

‌



In a post on Truth Social on Saturday evening local time, the President told the world that the United States will hold off on launching any further attack as the 'perimeters' of a deal has been agreed. He says this would include the Strait of the Hormuz being totally reopened and Iran committing to 'ending its nuclear threat'.

‌



Trump claims Israel is also committed to forming a deal and not furthering the escalation of the conflict.

‌



The post on Truth Social stated: "The U.S.A. is locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran, at levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II.

View 3 Images Donald Trump on the golf course (Image: Getty)

"Despite this, we have just been asked by Iran, and other Middle Eastern Countries, to hold off any attack in that the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to. This would include the Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran’s nuclear threat.

‌



"Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL.

"The Country of Israel joins me in this commitment. Get to work, everybody, and get it DONE. Thank you for your attention to this matter! President DONALD J. TRUMP."

It comes as Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the kingdom’s de facto leader, expressed in a phone call with Trump his concerns about the US potentially escalating the conflict with Iran, according to a person familiar with the leaders’ discussion.

‌



View 3 Images President Donald Trump meets Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in the Oval Office of the White House, Tuesday, Nov. 18, 2025, in Washington. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci) (Image: AP)

The Saudis, according to the person briefed on the substance of the call but not authorized to comment publicly, are concerned that if the US targets Iran’s energy infrastructure or carries out massive strikes on other key infrastructure that Tehran could respond by carrying out attacks on the kingdom’s and other Gulf countries’ energy infrastructure.

The crown prince during Saturday’s call sought clarity from Trump on what potential new action he’s weighing to take against Iran, the person said.

Article continues below

A White House official, who was not authorised to comment publicly and requested anonymity, confirmed the leaders spoke on Saturday but did not offer any detail about the substance of their conversation.

News.title: Tourist plane crashes in Peru killing all 13 people onboard as Aerodiana airline breaks silence
News.content:
Tourist plane crashes in Peru killing all 13 people onboard as Aerodiana airline breaks silence

Aerodiana airline has extended its heartfelt condolences to the families of the 13 people who tragically died in a plane crash just outside the city of Nazca in Peru

View 3 Images All 13 people on the plane died (Image: X/@AZ_Intel_)

Aerodiana airline has issued a statement following a crash in Peru which killed all 13 people on board the small plane.

‌



The plane crashed into a field on Saturday just outside the city of Nazca killing 13 people, local authorities said.

‌



In a statement on Facebook, Nazca's municipal government said the plane was taking tourists on a sightseeing flight of the Nazca Lines, a group of extensive geoglyphs scraped into the desert around Nazca hundreds of years ago by Peru's Indigenous inhabitants. The lines form images of animals that can only be fully appreciated from planes or viewing towers.

‌



View 3 Images The scene of the crash (Image: X/@AZ_Intel_)

Suffolk wildfire: National Trust launches emergency appeal to restore Dunwich Heath READ MORE :

Mum suffers life-changing injuries and unable to work after tripping on pothole READ MORE :

Nazca's government said the plane departed from the nearby city of Ica and was operated by Peru vian company Aerodiana. On its website the airline says that it has offered scenic flights over the Nazca lines for the past 14 years, using Cessna Grand Caravan planes.

In a statement, Peru 's Ministry for Trade and Tourism said that 11 “foreign tourists” and two crew members were on the plane that crashed Saturday. State news agency Agencia Andina reported that two German, two Spanish and seven Italian tourists were on the plane.

‌



Peru vian authorities said the accident is under investigation.

Municipalidad Provincial de Nasca wrote in a statement on Facebook: "The Provincial Municipality of Nasca expresses its deep sorrow for the accident involving the aircraft of Aerodiana and extends its heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased.

"The official information contradicted with the DGAC, the aircraft was based in the city of Pisco and took off from its airport to carry out a tourist flight over the Lines and Geoglifos of Nasca. The Provincial Municipality of Nasca provided the corresponding support since the emergency was reported."

‌



View 3 Images The company has been operating for 18 years (Image: X/@AZ_Intel_)

In a statement posted in Spanish on their Facebook page a spokesperson for Aerodiana said: "AERODIANA expresses its deepest sorrow for the tragic accident that occurred today during a tourist overflight operation in the Nazca Lines area.

"In this moment of immense grief, we extend our most sincere condolences and solidarity to the families and loved ones of the deceased. We share in their grief with respect and are fully prepared to provide any necessary support. "From the outset, we have been cooperating with the competent authorities and providing all the information necessary for the development of the corresponding investigations. "Throughout our 18 years of operation, we have maintained a constant commitment to the safety of our passengers and crews. Therefore, this event deeply affects us and reaffirms our willingness to cooperate fully and responsibly in everything required by the authorities. "We also inform you that the company will evaluate its flight schedule in accordance with the provisions of the competent authorities. We appreciate the understanding of our passengers, partners, and community during this difficult time."

Article continues below

None of the victims have been formerly identified yet.

News.title: 'Multiple people' dead after gunman opens fire at In-N-Out Burger restaurant
News.content:
'Multiple people' dead after gunman opens fire at In-N-Out Burger restaurant

An eyewitness has stated that they saw a person with an AR-style rifle emerging from the drive-thru on Saturday before the horrific incident unfolded in Southern Idaho

View 2 Images This still image captured from video by a witness shows the scene of a shooting that started at an In-N-Out Burger restaurant, Saturday, Aug. 1, 2026 in Twin Falls, Idaho. (Image: Kevin Bell Jr. via AP)

Multiple people have died after a gunman walked into a fast food restaurant and opened fire.

‌



The horrific incident unfolded at an In-N-Out Burger restaurant in southern Idaho on Saturday afternoon, August 1 - it has left multiple people dead and others injured.

‌



The shooter, who was carrying an AR-style rifle, was among the dead, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said in a news conference. The shooter’s identity and motive is not yet known.

‌



According to the Sun, at least three people have lost their lives after the shooting with at least five people injured.

“We believe the threat to the community is over,” Hicks said. He added that he did not yet know exactly how many were killed or wounded, and officials were still in the process of notifying next of kin. “It was a very chaotic scene.”

View 2 Images A view of the suspected gunman in Idaho

‌



The city spokesperson, Josh Palmer, told NBC News that he expects "that number (those injured) to increase."

Lane Koehn, 34, said he was at a stoplight near the In-N-Out when he saw a person with an AR-style rifle emerge from the drive-thru. A man with a pistol started firing at the shooter.

He then saw someone in an In-N-Out uniform drag a person, also uniformed, bleeding from a gunshot wound in her chest across the parking lot. The employee, Koehn and the man with the pistol stayed until paramedics arrived for her.

‌



“She was pretty bad off, but I don’t know. I hope she made it,” Koehn said.

St. Luke’s Magic Valley spokesperson Taylor Marschner said in a statement that the medical centre was “working closely with law enforcement and emergency responders as they manage the situation.”

Twin Falls, a city of about 56,000 people, is about 130 miles (205 kilometers) southeast of Boise and about 75 miles (120 kilometers) north of the Nevada border.

Article continues below

Idaho Governor Brad Little wrote on X: “Idahoans, join me in keeping the Twin Falls community in your prayers as law enforcement and first responders respond to an active shooter situation near In-N-Out.

“Please avoid the area and follow directions from law enforcement as they work to keep everyone safe.”

News.title: Moscow explosion: Three dead and 21 injured after bomb detonates at busy restaurant
News.content:
Moscow explosion: Three dead and 21 injured after bomb detonates at busy restaurant

Three people have been killed as more fight for their live in hospital after a homemade explosive device was detonated at an Italian restaurant in Moscow, Russia

View 3 Images The bomber, a security guard and a visitor to the restaurant are said to have died (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

An explosion at a restaurant in ‌central ⁠Moscow has killed at least three people, according to Russian state media.

‌



At least 21 people were injured in the explosion with some left fighting for their lives as investigators, forensic experts and emergency services continue working at the scene. A homemade explosive device was detonated at the Italian eatery in Kudrinskaya Square.

‌



The bomber, as well as a security guard and a diner, died in the blast at the trendy Balzi Rossi. The National Anti-Terrorist Committee said a woman carrying explosives attempted to enter the restaurant but was stopped. The device then went off, killing the woman, the guard and a visitor.

‌



View 3 Images Police take security measures at the scene in Moscow (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

The blast happened at around 8pm local time (5pm UK). The attack is still being investigated, the Moscow Investigative Committee told the RIA news agency, who released a video showing heavily armed law enforcement officers at the scene. Roads nearby have been closed off to members of the public.

Witnesses said they saw people leaving covered in blood following the explosion. Authorities have not named those killed or injured and have yet say who they thought might have been responsible.

‌



Those injured in the attack had received wounds of varying seriousness, according to police.

View 3 Images The restaurant is located in one of the city's famous Stalin-era skyscrapers (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

The exclusive restaurant's website stated that it was closed on Saturday for private event on its outdoor terrace.

Article continues below

Balzi Rossi is located at the base of the Kudrinskaya Square Building, one of Moscow’s Stalinist skyscrapers, which were built in the 1950s.

“We’re all fine, and our restaurant and kitchen are in perfect condition; there was just a minor issue at the restaurant entrance,” Balzi Rossi chef Carmine Alfieri said on Instagram without elaborating further.

Dozens of cyclists had been gathering nearby for an evening ride.

News.title: Several injured as 'overcrowded' North London festival halted and police called
News.content:
Several injured as 'overcrowded' North London festival halted and police called

The Ghana Party in the Park in Barnet was 'temporarily paused', according to organisers.

View Image Police were called to the scene (file photo) (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

A cultural festival in London was halted this evening (Saturday) after several people were injured. The Ghana Party in the Park in Barnet was 'temporarily paused', according to organisers.

‌



Police said that they attended the site of the event at Copthall Playing Fields due to an 'overcrowding issue'. Several people had been injured, police added, but none of the injuries are life-threatening in nature.

‌



Met Police in Barnet said: "Officers are at Copthall Playing Fields where Ghana Party in the Park has been cancelled after an overcrowding issue at the entrance saw several people sustain non-life threatening injuries. Speculation about a stabbing is inaccurate. Please help us by avoiding the area."

‌



Organisers of the event posted on social media: "Due to a major incident at the festival site, the event has been temporarily paused. Please do not travel to or come to the festival site until further notice.

"The emergency services and relevant authorities are currently managing the situation. We kindly ask everyone to stay away from the area to allow them to carry out their work safely.

Article continues below

"We will provide further updates as soon as more information becomes available. Thank you for your patience, understanding, and cooperation."

News.title: Naples earthquake recap: Italy struck by 4.7 magnitude quake as rocks crush cars
News.content:
The quake has caused a massive landslide in Pozzuoli

Residents in Naples have been left terrified after a powerful earthquake caused damage to the Italian city - it registered at 4.7 magnitude

A powerful earthquake struck southern Italy, causing damage in the city of Naples.

The 4.7 magnitude quake has left neighbourhoods without power, and residents are taking to the streets in fear. It occurred just before 8pm (local time).

According to data released by the INGV (National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology), the magnitude was 4.7. Power outages have been reported from Pizzofalcone to Fuorigrotta, and there has been a massive landslide in Pozzuoli.

Images show buildings have crumbled, with debris crushing cars.

Thank you for following our live blog. It has now ended.

News.title: Golden retriever defies vets to survive FIVE surgeries after he's bitten by a snake
News.content:
Golden retriever defies vets to survive FIVE surgeries after he's bitten by a snake

Beloved puppy Kobi suddenly fell ill after going out for walk with his owner Roma Morgan, who had no idea her pet had been bitten by an adder in Aberystwyth, west Wales

View 4 Images Kobi was bitten by an adder in Aberystwyth, Wales (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

A fearless Golden retriever shook off five surgeries to defy vets after being bitten by an adder.

‌



Kobi had been walking through long grass when he suddenly became "very lethargic". His owner Roma Morgan rushed the seven-month-old pup to her local vets, where he had blood tests and painkillers but continued to fall ill and and cried when touched.

‌



It was only when they shaved Kobi's swollen neck that a traumatic puncture wound was discovered - and her pet was then taken to another vet for a second opinion and given anti-venom. But over the next 10 months, he underwent five separate operations and 90 wound dressing changes with treatment costing more than £8,000.

‌



Roma, of Penparcau, near Aberystwth, west Wales, says she and husband Steve are "forever grateful" to the vets who "gave him the care he needed" She is now warning others of the risks of adder bites to their dogs but says seeing Kobi finally recovered brought her so much joy.

Millions of UK dog owners issued crucial garden advice by Monty Don READ MORE :

View 4 Images Owner Roma Morgan rushed her dog to the vet where he had blood tests and painkillers (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

She said: "It was best feeling. Seeing him running and swimming makes it all worthwhile. He's our little hero." Friends began a fundraising page to help Roma and Steve pay for Kobi's treatement in June last year.

‌



The page read: "Kobi, just a curious baby golden retriever, whilst playing in the river was bitten by an adder. He didn't make a fuss, and nobody witnessed it.

"He became very poorly, very quickly, and eventually it was realised that he'd been bitten by a venomous snake. It was already at advanced stages in his system by this time.

"A long, heartbreaking fight to save Kobi began from that moment. Roma and her husband Steve sourced anti venom and drove away to collect it.

‌



View 4 Images Kobi needed months to recover from his injuries (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

"The veterinarians began the slow process of fixing their boy, bearing in mind that he would not suffer more than he needed to. It was feared that his organs would fail, but he pulled through with intensive care.

"His skin perished and he has bravely endured multiple surgeries which will continue until all the fluid build ups are cleared and his skin is healed. He is a champion, he survived on love."

‌



Adders are the only venomous snake native to the UK and are protected by the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

View 4 Images His owner is now warning dog owners about the dangers of adders (Image: WALES NEWS SERVICE)

Warning about stomach complaint that can be fatal

Last month, a vet warned dog owners to bring their pets into their local practice immediately if they notice one change in their body - as it could be fatal. It can sometimes be difficult to know if and when you should take your pet to the vets, and if an issue is a genuine emergency.

‌



In a TikTok video, vets at Green Pastures Vets in Weston-super-Mare, Somerset, ran through two scenarios that commonly arise in dogs, weighing in on whether each one constitutes an emergency.

One of the vets asked: "Kathleen, emergency or not, a dog shaking for no obvious reason?" Kathleen replied: "Yes, they could be fitting, always better to just be sure."

According to the PDSA, if a dog suffers a GDV (Gastric dilatation-volvulus), they will likely require surgery to untwist their stomach. However, tragically, even with intervention, some GDVs prove fatal.

Article continues below

The PDSA said: "Any dog can develop a GDV but it's most common in giant and deep chested breeds such as as German Shepherds, Great Danes, Saint Bernards and Dobermanns.

"It's more common in dogs that have a parent or full sibling (brother/sister) that have had a GDV, and tends to mostly affect middle-aged to older dogs."

News.title: US citizens issued 'be prepared' Middle East warning as Donald Trump threatens Iran
News.content:
US citizens issued 'be prepared' Middle East warning as Donald Trump threatens Iran

A new travel advisory has been issued for 10 countries in the Middle East by the US State Department

View Image The US is continuing to strike Iran as the conflict continues (file) (Image: US MARINE CORPS/AFP via Getty Images)

The US has warned its citizens to prepare for a possible evacuation from the Middle East following Donald Trump's latest threat to launch strikes against Iran.

‌



The State Department has issued a fresh advisory covering 10 Middle East countries: the United Arab Emirates (UAE), I srael, Oman, Qatar, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain and Egypt.

‌



It called on Americans in the region to "exercise heightened vigilance" and "be prepared to depart should there be escalation", while also warning of "flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions", reports the Daily Express.

‌



The advisory mentioned that the "Iranian regime is unpredictable, as seen by its recent decisions to attack areas in the region without warning or to expand attacks to areas not previously targeted (such as Egypt)".

Posting on X, the alert said: "Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions. Some airlines in the region have postponed resumption of earlier flight schedules; others have cancelled some routes.

‌



"Americans in the region should consider departing, or be prepared to depart should there be escalation. Americans outside the Middle East should seriously reconsider travel to and through the region.

"Those who do travel to or from the region should monitor information about airport and airline operations. U.S. diplomatic facilities, including outside the Middle East, have been targeted. Iran and groups supportive of Iran may target other U.S. interests overseas or at locations associated with the United States and Americans throughout the world, including U.S. businesses and other institutions."

On Saturday, Major General Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's wartime military command, declared: "The United States is moving at an accelerating pace to fan the flames of a full-scale regional war."

Article continues below

He continued: "It is hereby stated explicitly: Muslim countries must, with foresight, monitor America's crimes and reconsider their cooperation and alignment with the US.

"Otherwise, any country that makes itself a defensive shield for criminal, aggressor America will burn in the fire of war."

News.title: A bruising 24 hours - what next for Fifa and under-pressure Infantino?
News.content:
The quickest route for Infantino's exit would be for the Swiss to resign, like his predecessor Sepp Blatter did in 2015.

But Infantino still retains support and he could try to hold out until March, when he is up for re-election for a fourth and final term as president.

What other avenues are open?

The Fifa Council could try to force Infantino's hand through an emergency meeting.

Such a gathering would be triggered if 19 of the 37 Fifa Council members call for one.

Uefa has nine members, AFC has seven, Concacaf five, Africa has six, Conmebol five and Oceania three. It is completed by Infantino and secretary general Mattias Grafstrom.

BBC Sport understands there are some doubts that the 19 votes could be achieved.

If they do get to 19, the meeting must take place within two weeks and the Fifa Council could call on Infantino to tender his resignation. But he could simply refuse to do so.

It would, however, add further pressure.

The next step would be an extraordinary congress of the 211 Fifa member associations, which would be held if one-fifth, or 43 associations, "make such a request in writing".

So Uefa, which has 55 nations, can trigger the extraordinary congress whenever it so wishes.

That would take a minimum of two months from the point it is triggered, but more likely three months, and there is no guarantee of success.

In effect, it would be a de facto election without there being another candidate as 106 votes would be needed to pass the vote of no confidence.

Uefa has 55, Africa 54, Asia 46, Concacaf 35, Oceania 11 and Conmebol 10.

Africa, Conmebol and Oceania have not criticised Infantino's plan.

So could Uefa get to 106? In total, 136 countries officially rejected the investment plan, but voting to reject an idea is not the same as voting to kick Infantino out.

Of the 136, Qatar have already publicly backed him and Mexico have distanced themselves from the joint Concacaf statement.

Which leaves finding a suitable candidate to fight the election in March.

Infantino stood unopposed when he was re-elected in 2019 and 2023 and if someone wants to battle him for the position, the deadline to announce their candidacy is 18 November.

News.title: Emotional Kerr delivers moment Glasgow 2026 has waited for with men's mile gold
News.content:
There were no pacers. No wave lights. No declarations about what time he would run or what record he would beat. This was a Saturday night scrap - Glasgow rules - and Josh Kerr wasn't going to let anyone beat him in that fight.

Not his childhood pal and Scotland team-mate Jake Wightman. Not the Australian prodigy Cam Myers. Not the former Olympic silver medallist Timothy Cheruiyot.

This Commonwealth Games men's mile was his race, in his country, in front of his people. This gold medal really meant something.

Kerr's explosion of joy after he crossed the line and swaddled himself in a Saltire - having conducted the crowd during his final few strides - made that clear.

And so did his halting attempts to sing along with Flower of Scotland, the 28-year-old repeatedly stopping to bite his lip before wiping away tears from each eye.

"We rush through these moments so quickly," Kerr told BBC Sport Scotland, having spent the best part of 45 minutes doing selfies and signatures. "So I was just telling myself to slow down.

"In my head, I was flashing through all the hard moments and realising that I've come a long way. And to have Flower of Scotland playing versus the GB national anthem, it's just different. Not many times in my career I'll ever have that."

News.title: Three killed after bomb detonated at Moscow restaurant, state media say
News.content:
At least three people have been killed and 21 injured after a homemade explosive device was detonated at an Italian restaurant in Moscow, Russian state media quotes security officials as saying.

The blast happened at around 20:00 local time (17:00 GMT) on Kudrinskaya square near the city centre.

The National Anti-Terrorist Committee (NAK) said a woman carrying the explosives tried to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard. The device detonated, killing the woman, the guard and a visitor to the restaurant.

The restaurant, located in one of Moscow's famous Stalin-era skyscrapers, had been holding a private function.

Authorities have not disclosed the guest list or said anything about who they believe was the target of the attack.

Witnesses said they saw people being brought out covered in blood after the explosion.

Initial reports said the blast happened in the establishment's kitchen but the restaurant later issued a statement saying "there was a problem outside".

Roads around the square were briefly closed. Dozens of cyclists had been gathering nearby for an evening ride through the city but the event was cancelled.

Video released by Russia's RIA news agency showed heavily armed law enforcement officers at the scene, which had been closed off to members of the public.

In recent years, several senior Russian military figures have been assassinated in and around the Russian capital. Moscow has blamed Kyiv for those attacks.

News.title: Does Love Island UK need to pull the US version for a chat?
News.content:
What's your dream Love Island series on paper?

Some watch for the heartwarming romances, like Molly-Mae Hague and Tommy Fury falling for each other back in 2019, while others prefer intense dramas - we see you 2022 winners Ekin-Su CÃ¼lcÃ¼loÄlu and Davide Sanclimenti.

Others tune in for exciting challenges like Snog, Marry, Pie or the ones which literally send heart rates soaring.

For most, it's a mix of all of the above, and it's a balance TV producers have been trying to strike for years with the original UK series, as well as a host of spin-offs and international editions.

It's no secret that Love Island UK linear viewing figures have dropped from their 2019 heyday, with streaming and social media becoming more of a focus.

Across the pond the US edition has been reaching new heights, with the latest eighth series ranked as the number one reality show for five weeks in the States across all streaming platforms, according to its streamer Peacock. , external

It also had an injection of star power as US celebrity fans, including Lizzo, Demi Lovato and Kesha, sent messages of support to the finalists, while rapper Megan Thee Stallion has become a regular guest.

BBC Newsbeat has been speaking to fans, commentators and an ex-Islander to see what they feel the UK edition could learn from the US version to regain its spark.

News.title: I had a vasectomy in my 20s after the trauma of my sons' births
News.content:
Because he was asking for a vasectomy at such a young age, Sam had prepared for the questions his doctor was going to ask him: Don't you think you're too young to know you don't want kids? Could you change your mind in future? You do know reversals are expensive and aren't always successful?

"[The doctor] actually said he had very recently changed his view," says Sam. "And that, if I had come in half a year earlier, he would have turned me away instantly."

His vasectomy took place a couple of months after he first contacted the clinic.

The questions from Sam's doctor were designed to ensure he was making a decision he could live with; men under 30 are more likely to regret a vasectomy, according to guidance from NHS Scotland, external.

Dr Sarah Salkeld, a former GP who is now a medical director for MSI Reproductive Choices, a group of clinics offering various contraceptives to NHS and private patients, says a vasectomy is "very safe and effective".

But she cautions it is important for men to "really think about" whether a vasectomy is right for them.

"We offer everyone counselling to talk about it if they want to, just toâ¦ make sure they've got all the information they need to make that decision."

She says reversals are not routinely available on the NHS as there are strict criteria for having one.

The NHS website points out that other forms of contraception, external are available to men, including condoms and the fertility awareness method - avoiding sex or using condoms on the days when their female partner is most fertile.

Sam told his doctor that, while he loved kids and had a happy childhood himself, he wanted to stay focused on his job as a sound designer for video games.

News.title: Solitude as a new aspirational lifestyle: 'We are not lonely'
News.content:
It's a Friday night. A young woman trudges back to her apartment after a day of work. She enters a spotless kitchen, unloads a bag of groceries, and unwraps a frozen pizza before sliding it in the oven.

What follows is a nightly routine that is almost meditative in its mundanity: she lights a candle and gazes briefly at the snow-covered landscape outside her window, piles a premade salad onto a plate with the pizza, and settles on her sofa to eat in front of the TV.

The tagline that accompanies the scene reads: "POV you're a childfree and single girl that has no friends and lives alone so this is how you spend your Friday night."

At the centre of the video â which has amassed seven million views on TikTok â is Lana Isa, a software sales manager in her 20s based in Toronto.

In addition to chronicling her nightly self-care routines, she takes her almost 400,000 followers across TikTok and Instagram on late-night fast food drives, reading sessions perched on a rock by the lake, even a saga of getting locked out of her apartment in the middle of the night.

Isa is part of a growing, albeit niche corner of the internet where content creators, many of them women, share their daily rituals of living alone, choosing to spotlight a lifestyle that prioritises peace and solitude - the antithesis of social media excess.

For Isa, unveiling the "no friends" aspect of her life was less of a tagline, but the "reality" she had been living for several years.

News.title: Spider-Man fans hail Brand New Day as Holland's best yet
News.content:
Fans have been queuing outside cinemas to catch the latest Spider-Man film, with many hailing it as a spectacular return for the web-slinging superhero.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day marks Tom Holland's fourth standalone adventure as the protagonist and hero Peter Parker.

Picking up after the events of Spider-Man: No Way Home, the film follows Parker as he devotes his time to protecting New York City while adjusting to a life in which everyone, including his closest friends, has forgotten who he is.

The fourth Spider-Man film is director Destin Daniel Cretton's second project in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), having previously been at the helm of Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings.

Appearing together in the same film for a second time this summer, Holland reprises the role alongside his wife Zendaya, who stars once again as MJ.

There is also a return for Jon Bernthal's Punisher, making his first appearance in an MCU feature film, and an introduction to the MCU for Sadie Sink, whose role in the plot has been kept firmly under wraps.

News.title: Ginger hair portraits show unexpected 'golden thread' connecting Americans
News.content:
For Kieran Dodds, photographing people with red hair has become something of an obsession over the past decade.

The 45-year-old, from Edinburgh, who is himself a "proud ginger", began taking pictures in his homeland in 2013 as part of a series examining Scottish identity.

His interest in the subject soon took him to other ginger hotspots such the Russian city of Perm and Jamaica's Treasure Beach.

His 2020 book Gingers spanned the world but after its release he notice there was a "huge gap".

"I realised I didn't have any American citizens," Kieran told the BBC.

"Then all these people got in touch."

News.title: William and Kate bring children to second last day of Commonwealth Games
News.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales have brought their three children to watch some of the final sporting events at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Cheering crowds at the city's OVO Hydro were treated to exhilarating performances in the netball semi-finals where the family watched New Zealand's 61-54 win over England.

Known as the Duke and Duchess of Rothesay while in Scotland, the couple also spent time meeting athletes, staff and volunteers during a slightly blustery visit to the venue on the River Clyde.

They then made their way to the Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome - where they chatted to British cyclist Dame Laura Kenny and sat one row behind another Olympic cycling champion, Sir Chris.

News.title: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja killed in Pakistan avalanche, his company says
News.content:
Purja's death was also confirmed by Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who said that "the tragic death of six Nepalese and four other foreign climbers, including world record holder Nirmal Purja, in the Karakoram mountain range of Pakistan, has shocked us".

"The history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring," the prime minister added.

In a statement, Purja's older brother Kamal wrote: "It is with the heaviest heart that I share the devastating news that my beloved younger brother, Nirmal 'Nimsdai' Purja, and the other climbers are no longer with us.

"Although our hearts are broken, we are incredibly proud of you. Your legacy will live forever," he added.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a post on X: "Incredibly sad to learn of the passing of Nirmal (Nims) Purja and those he was climbing with.

"He was an inspirational man who served in our Armed Forces for many years - and whose incredible mountaineering adventures are known the world over."

Naila Kiani, a spokesperson for the Alpine Club of Pakistan which is involved in the rescue efforts, told BBC's Newshour programme that Purja had led many expeditions that she was on.

Praising his leadership skills, she described him as a "very experienced climber and fearless".

Kiani said the Alpine Club would only announce his death once the body has been recovered - but she added that "we are fearing them all dead".

She also said rescuers had seen some bodies - but were yet to reach them.

Teams in Pakistan have been searching for the climbers on the world's 12th-highest summit after an avalanche on the 8,047m (26,400ft) peak in the Karakoram range.

The multinational climbing group was being led by Purja. Also known as Nims, he rose to prominence in 2019 when he climbed all 14 of the world's mountains with peaks above 8,000m in 189 days - smashing the previous record by more than seven years.

He became widely known following a Netflix documentary chronicling his journey, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, released two years later.

At the time, he said: "It has been a gruelling but humbling six months, and I hope to have proven that anything is possible with some determination, self-belief and positivity."

Purja served in the British military for 16 years, 10 of which were spent in the special forces, and he was awarded an MBE by the late Queen in 2018 for his achievement in extreme high-altitude mountaineering.

Purja, who lived with his wife and three-year-old daughter in Hampshire in southern England, said he was also the first Gurkha to climb Everest while serving in the British military.

In his last post on X, published on Monday, he said he had not intended to climb Broad Peak.

"Initially, the plan was to climb just G2," Purja wrote, referring to Gasherbrum II, another peak in the Karakoram mountain range.

But right before he set off for Pakistan, he realised that if he also managed to climb Broad Peak while he was there, he would have only one more mountain to conquer before becoming the "first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen."

An eight-thousander is a mountain that rises more than 8,000m above sea level.

"This wasn't planned," Purja wrote. "But opportunities don't scream: they whisper to those already working in silence."

"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down. I take zero mountains for granted," he wrote.

Broad Peak is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for climbers. The first successful ascent was in 1957, when an Austrian expedition reached the summit.

Since then, many more have climbed the mountain, but dozens have lost their lives.

One of Broad Peak's deadliest years was 2013, when at least six fatalities were recorded.

News.title: Peak District's rebrand deal brings in cash - but also criticism
News.content:
A deal between Peak District bosses and car firm Skoda to put up temporary signs welcoming tourists to "the Peaq District" in honour of the firm's new electric model has given the park authority's coffers a welcome boost.

However, it has also sparked protests from campaigners and residents unhappy about the commercial aspect of the arrangement.

One campaigner said: "If national parks are prepared to sell their very name to the highest bidder, then we're already on the path to industrial extraction of the most protected landscapes."

Park bosses have defended the "fantastic" deal and said the partnership brought in extra funds for conservation and heritage work.

With national parks continuing to grapple with funding pressures, could the partnership be a sign of things to come for the Peak District and beyond?

News.title: Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism row defends his work
News.content:
A Cambridge University professor has defended his academic work after finding himself at the centre of a plagiarism row.

The row erupted after another academic - self-defined "race realist" Nathan Cofnas, who was sacked from his Cambridge role in 2024 - said he found numerous instances of plagiarism in Prof Jason Arday's work and questioned some of his stated achievements.

While some critics say the treatment of Arday, who is black, has been motivated by racism, others have said the claims of plagiarism were legitimate.

Arday admitted errors in his work, telling the Times, external in an interview on Saturday that he was accountable for those mistakes but that "what I am not is a liar".

He told the newspaper: "There has been, since I arrived at Cambridge, a very well orchestrated and co-ordinated campaign to unseat me from my position."

He argued this was "racially motivated" and that he had become a "lightning rod" for criticism of diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) policy.

Arday said some errors in his early academic work was because of his autism, as he relied on using mimicry to make sense of information, and that similar scrutiny would find similar errors in work by other academics.

"We're talking about academia here. I didn't murder somebody. I think the cruelty that I've experienced and the positioning of me as this kind of liar and fantasist is totally unacceptable," he told the newspaper.

In 2023, the then 37-year-old sociologist became the youngest ever black professor at Cambridge, telling the BBC at the time his work focused on neurodivergence and race in education.

He was diagnosed with autism and global development delay in his early years, to which his being unable to speak until the age of 11 and unable to read or write until 18 was attributed.

Arday worked as a PE teacher before earning his doctorate at Liverpool John Moores University and going on to teach at Roehampton, Durham and Glasgow.

News.title: Suffolk fire 'stable' and fundraiser set up
News.content:
The blaze that has devastated heathland in Suffolk is now "stable" but crews have continued to tackle hotspots on what is the fourth day since the flames took hold.

The fire affecting RSPB Minsmere and Dunwich Heath started at about 17:00 BST on Wednesday and engulfed 371 acres (150 hectares) at its height - equivalent to the size of 210 football pitches.

Wildlife habitats of some of the UK's rarest species have been destroyed.

The National Trust has launched a fundraiser to help the habitats "recover and thrive in a changing climate".

Meanwhile, some local people have started returning to normal life.

A scheduled market went ahead at nearby Westleton earlier, which an organiser said was the chance for people to take their minds off recent events.

News.title: Wicker Man sequel director Justin Hardy dies aged 61
News.content:
British filmmaker Justin Hardy, who directed a sequel to his late father Robin's 1973 cult horror classic The Wicker Man, has died aged 61.

His family said Hardy died on Friday night after suffering a heart attack, remembering him as "a man of family, of boundless creativity" and "so full of life right to the end".

A Bafta and Emmy nominated writer and director, Hardy was known for the documentary Children of the Wicker Man in 2024, made with his brother Dominic, which chronicled the legacy of their father's iconic film.

He had just completed production on Wrath of the Gods, the concluding chapter to the Wicker Man trilogy, which was due to premiere in London later this month.

Hardy also directed historical films and documentaries for the BBC, Channel 4 and CNN, including Princes In The Tower, Trafalgar Battle Surgeon, The Relief Of Belsen and Spanish Flu: The Forgotten Fallen.

His family said they were "devastated" by his death and "heartbroken" Hardy would not be able to see Wrath of the Gods open.

Dominic described his brother as having "an incredible appetite for life".

"We've lost him and we've lost that larger-than-life presence looking over us all," he said. "He really became a filmmaker his own right."

Dominic also praised Hardy's work on his last film as "incredibly beautiful", adding it was "a great satisfaction to him" to have made something new.

The Wicker Man, starring Christopher Lee, is the story of a police officer sent to a remote Scottish island community to investigate the disappearance of a local girl.

Wrath of the Gods was inspired by recently discovered scripts and storyboards by Hardy's late father Robin, marking the end of the trilogy that began with The Wicker Man and the 2011 follow-up The Wicker Tree.

Hardy, who also taught screenwriting at University College London, is survived by his wife Larissa, and their four children.

News.title: Manhunt after prisoner escapes from van outside court
News.content:
A manhunt is under way after a prisoner escaped from a van taking him to a court appearance.

Stephen Grzyb, 22, was being transported by contractor GEOAmey from Belle Vale custody suite to Liverpool Magistrates' Court to face burglary charges on Saturday.

As the van arrived outside the court building, at around 10:00 BST, Grzyb was able to flee and ran off down Red Cross Street towards the Strand.

Merseyside Police said: "Assisting him in any way will bring police to your own door, so it is not an association worth keeping."

News.title: Boaters race against clock as drained canals close
News.content:
Boaters are racing against the clock to beat canal closures as waterways run dry due to extreme heat.

Some channels connecting large parts of the Midlands and the North of England have lost several inches of water, leaving narrowboats stuck and those already on the canals facing being stranded miles from home for weeks on end.

Campaigner George Seward said he was getting up at 05:00 BST and cruising until dark to get his narrowboat through the Atherstone flight of locks, after a sudden closure was announced.

"They're unlikely to be open again for many weeks and I want to make sure I get through that flight so I can get my boat safely home," he said.

The locks on the Coventry Canal in Warwickshire are due to shut on Tuesday morning, with last entry on Monday afternoon, as the Canal and River Trust (CRT) tries to conserve dwindling supplies.

For Seward, who is Midlands regional chair of the Association of Waterways Cruising Clubs, the deadline is the difference between getting his boat home to Hinckley in Leicestershire and being potentially marooned for an unspecified period.

A fast-moving wildfire driven by strong winds and high temperatures swept across northwest Spokane on Saturday before jumping the Spokane River and prompting the evacuation of thousands of people.

The Old Trails Fire started around noon, burning brush and grass in an open area, but quickly spread north and east toward residential areas. Cars lined the roads as people fled their homes, and orange and red flames were visible from the highway.

The blaze sent a plume of smoke billowing over the region, and as of the evening almost 4 square miles (10 square kilometers) of terrain had been burned, said Courtney James, spokesperson for the Washington State Department of Natural Resources.

The cause was under investigation.

“We urge residents of Spokane to heed evacuation orders and to stay alert to changing conditions and evacuations as they are rapidly changing,” James said.

Some structures were lost but officials did not yet have a solid count, said Jessica Watson, a DNR spokesperson for the fire. Firefighters had zero containment as of the evening and the wind continued to blow, she said.

Power company Avista said it implemented public safety shutoffs in the area due to elevated fire risk.

Gov. Bob Ferguson declared a state of emergency Saturday after unusually high temperatures and high winds exacerbated record wildfires across the state. The National Weather Service issued a “particularly dangerous situation” red flag alert for eastern Washington.

News.title: Idaho shooting updates: At least 3 dead and 2 injured in mass shooting at Idaho In-N-Out with casualties expected ‘to increase’
News.content:
( AP )

Read our Privacy notice

At least three people were killed and two others were injured in a mass shooting at an In-N-Out in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday, according to police and local officials.

The suspected shooter — an unidentified male — is dead, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said at a press conference. He described the scene as “tragic” and “chaotic.”

Joshua Palmer, a city spokesperson, told The Independent that the number of victims is expected to rise. “We want to emphasize that that number may change,” Palmer said. “That was just the first number we got.”

An “active shooter incident” was first reported at 4:29 p.m. ET at the In-N-Out on Blue Lakes Boulevard North. Police urged people to avoid the area, saying roads nearby would be closed as officers responded.

Shelter-in-place orders have since been lifted, Palmer said.

Hicks said the FBI is assisting the investigation, adding that information about the suspect and his motivations are expected to be revealed in the coming days.

Twin Falls, a city of about 56,000 people, is located roughly 130 miles southeast of Boise. There have been over 300 mass shootings in the U.S. this year, according to the Mass Shooter Tracker.

It was 1989, George H.W. Bush was in the White House, Madonna was on the radio and the country was in the grips of its last major measles outbreak - until today.

“People were scared to death to come to the city. I mean, schools canceled trips to the city. We were pulling one dead child out of the house after another,” pediatrician Dr. Paul Offit, an infectious disease expert at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia who was working in the city as cases exploded, told The Independent.

By the time the outbreak ended in 1991, there had been 55,467 cases and 166 deaths across the country, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention records show.

It was the worst outbreak the country had seen since the measles vaccine, which also targeted preventable illnesses mumps and rubella, was introduced in 1963. Public health officials blamed the crisis on low vaccine coverage.

Now - with more than 2,300 cases of the potentially-deadly disease in the U.S. and numbers rising weekly - there are no such vaccine barriers. But different obstacles exist: beginning with the White House.

open image in gallery College students stand in line for measles vaccinations at Georgia’s Auburn University in April 1989 - the year of the last major measles outbreak in the US - until today ( AP )

A skeptical White House

President Donald Trump’s public health agenda, spearheaded by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., has seen vaccine skeptics added to advisory panels and conspiracy theories about vaccines spoken about inside the federal government.

Trump himself has repeatedly claimed that young children are given 80 different vaccines.

"They give — I mean, for a little baby to be injected with that much fluid?" Trump told reporters in September. "Even beyond the actual ingredients, they have sometimes 80 different vaccines … It’s like you’re shooting up a horse."

The number of vaccinations before the age of 18 is typically between 30 to 50, doctors say.

The president has also recently pushed Kennedy - long known as a vaccine skeptic - to be more aggressive on cutting federal recommendations for annual child vaccines over the debunked ties to autism, The Wall Street Journal reported earlier this month.

open image in gallery Measles is a nasty virus that can lead to life-threatening brain swelling in children who are unvaccinated. Distrust in vaccines has been at the heart of America’s measles resurgence, with vaccine skepticism rising 15 percent since 2019 ( CDC )

open image in gallery President Donald Trump and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. have both made misleading comments that are skeptical of vaccines for children, including related to debunked ties between vaccines and autism ( Getty )

Last year, Kennedy said he directed the CDC to abandon its longstanding position that vaccines do not cause autism.

“The whole thing about ‘vaccines have been tested and there’s been this determination made,’ is just a lie,” he told The New York Times in November.

White House spokesperson Kush Desai also previously told the The Independent that people worried about “skyrocketing autism rates have long been ignored if not mocked.”

He added that the administration is “committed to leaving no stone unturned to finally address these concerns with Gold Standard Science.”

In vaccines we distrust

Distrust in vaccines in the U.S. came long before Trump but has grown in recent years because of misinformation that circulated online during the Covid-19 pandemic and in podcasts and social media since then.

That distrust has been at the heart of America’s measles resurgence, with vaccine skepticism rising 15 percent since 2019, according to a study from the University of Arkansas.

About one in five parents are not confident childhood vaccines have been tested enough or that the annual vaccine schedule for kids is safe, according to a 2025 Pew Research Center survey.

“Here we have a skeptical, mistrustful, conspiratorial population goaded on by people like Bobby Kennedy Jr. And now we have a very different kind of problem – and a dangerous one,” Dr. Irwin Redlener, co-founder of non-profit healthcare organization Children's Health Fund with the musician Paul Simon, told The Independent.

open image in gallery This map from the CDC shows measles cases across the U.S. so far this year. The states with the highest case levels are shown in darker blues and those with the lowest levels are shown in lighter blues ( CDC )

Since last year, there have been several large measles outbreaks affected by vaccine skepticism, including in a Mennonite community in West Texas and an evangelical Christian community in South Carolina. There were two child deaths reported in Texas.

Measles appears as an angry red rash dotting all areas of the skin, with cases causing a high fever, pink eye and runny nose. Normal cases typically last for a week or two but some who are infected develop a progressive brain disorder that is often fatal.

The virus spreads quickly through the air after an infected person coughs or sneezes - even if they are no longer in the room a couple of hours later.

Fortunately, the answer to stopping the spread is the same as it was 35 years ago: vaccines.

open image in gallery Ethan Turner holds his 14-month-old son, Niko, while he gets the measles vaccine at a clinic in Lubbock, Texas, in March 2025. Increased vaccination helped to end the measles outbreak in Texas last August ( Getty )

open image in gallery Medical workers assess a patient with symptoms of the measles in a parking lot in Spartanburg, South Carolina, in January. Spartanburg was the site of one of the nation’s biggest outbreaks since last year ( The Washington Post/Getty )

A deadly cost

During the last major outbreak, in 1991, Philadelphia saw 1,400 cases, with about a third in middle-class Christians, accounting for six deaths in under a year, according to Offit.

Religious exemptions to vaccines were legal in Pennsylvania, as remains the case across more than 40 states, and these communities “just didn’t believe in modern medicine,” he recalled.

“And you know, they believed in prayer. And if you prayed and your child died, then you hadn’t gotten close enough to God,” Offit said.

Several months into that surge, Philadelphia doctors were issued an order from a judge to vaccinate children, regardless of the parents’ wishes - something that hasn’t been done since. The decision helped stop cases in their tracks.

In states with other outbreaks, free vaccine clinics at universities played a role in slowing the spread of measles at a time when the jab wasn’t always without a cost. Georgia’s Auburn University, Illinois’s University of Chicago and Ohio’s Kent State University offered the shots free of charge.

Cost was the primary hurdle for children in the U.S. not getting vaccinated during the 1989 outbreak, according to the CDC. At the time shots cost over $30, a 1989 New York Times article reported.

Many low-income families also did not have access to primary care physicians who could give children vaccines, Redlener explained.

“[Back then it] was problems of access along with, ‘Oh, is it really serious, anyway?’” he said. More than half of children infected in the that outbreak had not been vaccinated.

It took a national effort to pull America out of the crisis. New guidelines for a second dose of the vaccine were released in 1989, giving Americans an added layer of protection from the virus. Two doses of the vaccine are 97 percent effective against infection, whereas one dose is 93 percent effective.

In 1993, President Bill Clinton’s administration launched the federal Vaccines for Children initiative, providing vaccines for kids whose parents who may have not been able to afford them.

By 2000, 76 percent of children in the U.S. had the measles vaccine - which helped stop the continuous spread of the disease for more than a year and brought cases to a record low.

'I think people don't remember measles'

Now, more than 90 percent of children have had their measles shots. But coverage needed to limit spread among kindergarteners is lower than it should be and has been declining since before the pandemic.

So an illness that many doctors thought they had resigned to history has come roaring back and as a far murkier and complex problem to solve.

“Now we have a challenge that none of us have formally been trained for. What do we do with recalcitrant, anti-science ideologues who have bought into the conspiracies being sold by the likes of Bobby Kennedy Jr.?” Redlener asked.

open image in gallery Incoming kindergartener Jeremy Conner, 5, reacts to a measles shot in Santa Ana, California, in August 2002. Measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000 ( Getty )

While Kennedy denied being anti-vaccine during his confirmation hearings to become health secretary, he’s also touted unconventional treatments for measles and previously falsely claimed that outbreaks were tied to the fact the vaccine didn’t offer lifelong protection. The measles vaccine offers lifelong protection, per the CDC.

“As long as we have a federal government that’s committed to promoting misinformation and conspiracy theories, it’s going to be very difficult to fix anything,” Redlener added.

In response to today's rising cases, HHS says Kennedy has been clear that vaccination is the most effective way to prevent infection and that the department has focused its response on supporting affected communities and strengthening local and state response.

"Under Secretary Kennedy's leadership, HHS has mounted an aggressive outbreak response, providing more than $8.5 million to states and local partners, expanding technical assistance, and surging CDC personnel and resources to support containment efforts where needed most,” Press Secretary Emily Hilliard told The Independent.

Offit believes the measles outbreaks will continue in an era of medical freedom, and as people believe they have the right to make their own health decisions and stop caring about the health of their neighbors.

Part of the problem is that people don’t remember past outbreaks, he said, and some younger doctors working at his hospital had never seen a measles case before.

“I think that not only did we eliminate the disease, we eliminated the memory of the disease. I think people don’t remember measles,” he said.

Police say multiple people died in a shooting at a southern Idaho In-N-Out fast food restaurant, and others were injured.

The shooter is also dead, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said.

The shooting was reported Saturday afternoon near a busy shopping area in Twin Falls.

Hicks said he did not have a number yet of how many were killed and injured. Officials were still in the process of notifying next of kin.

THIS IS A BREAKING NEWS UPDATE. AP’s earlier story follows below.

TWIN FALLS, Idaho (AP) — A shooting near a southern Idah shopping center left multiple people injured Saturday afternoon, authorities reported.

Twin Falls County Commissioner Brent Reinke said Sheriff Jack Johnson told him five people were hurt in the shooting, which started at an In-N-Out Burger restaurant.

While there were no immediate confirmations of deaths and details remained limited, Reinke said it was likely there were some fatalities. He added that the shooter “is also down.”

Reinke, who is also former prison chief for the Idaho Department of Corrections, said he learned of the incident just before 4 p.m. Multiple agencies responded.

“We’re loading people up, all the witnesses, and taking them to different locations for interviews,” Reinke said. “We should have a lot more information within the hour.”

Twin Falls police advised people to avoid the area as they closed roads.

St. Luke’s Magic Valley spokesperson Taylor Marschner said in a statement that the medical center was “working closely with law enforcement and emergency responders as they manage the situation.”

Twin Falls, a city of about 56,000 people, is about 130 miles (205 kilometers) southeast of Boise and about 75 miles (120 kilometers) north of the Nevada border.
