Three people have died and at least 21 more were injured after a homemade bomb carried by a woman exploded near a central Moscow restaurant on Saturday evening, Russian authorities said.

The explosion, which occurred at around 7.55pm local time (5.55pm BST), detonated near an upscale Italian restaurant located in one of Moscow’s seven Stalin-era skyscrapers at Kudrinkskaya Square, police said.

Russia’s Anti-Terrorism Committee said that an unidentified woman had tried to get ​into ⁠the restaurant, but was ‌stopped by a security guard, according to Russian news agencies.

open image in gallery Law enforcement officers stand guard at the site of an explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow ( Reuters )

Among the dead were the security guard, the woman, and another visitor, the committee added. They have not been named and there are no official theories about the perpetrator. Those injured had received wounds of varying seriousness, according to police.

The Kommersant daily newspaper cited sources who claimed that the bomb had been intended to maim and kill guests who were enjoying themselves outside on the restaurant’s summer terrace. The restaurant’s ‌website said the venue had ​been closed on Saturday for a private event, but it is unclear who was present.

More than four years into a full-scale war with Ukraine, Russia’s FSB security service said earlier this year that authorities would step up protection for high-ranking military officials after a series of assassinations and attempted killings which it blamed on Kyiv.

open image in gallery Law enforcement officers and emergency services personnel work at the site of an explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow ( Reuters )

In June, Vladimir Putin’s ammunition chief Damir Davydov was killed in a car bombing in Moscow.

But there has not yet been any suggestion that Saturday’s attack was linked to the Ukraine war, with Kremlin officials still to put forward any theories.

Russia’s state RIA news agency released video of heavily armed law enforcement officers at the scene, which was closed off from the public.

open image in gallery Police vehicles at the site of an explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow ( Reuters )

Russian state TV earlier speculated that the explosion may have been caused by a gas canister detonating, a theory which was later dropped.

Investigators and emergency services remain working at the scene.

The Baza online news outlet, which has good contacts with law enforcement, said the explosion had occurred at the upscale Balzi Rossi Italian restaurant.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Kerr wins by a mile: Scot claims Commonwealth gold to emulate Bannister
News.content:
For many the 100m is the Blue Riband event the one everyone wants to watch and the race that steals all the headlines. For these Commonwealth Games, however, tonight’s mile race is the one that has grabbed all the attention – and it is not hard to see why.

Josh Kerr, fresh from his new world record of 3:42.66 (a time that beat a mark that had stood since 1999) takes on fellow Scot Jake Wightman and Australia’s new superstar Cameron Myers. Three great runners over a distance that evokes sepia-tinted memories of Roger Bannister and the seminal four-minute mark.

Some of you may be wondering why the mile is back at an international event. Well, Seb Coe, the president of World Athletics and someone who broke the mile record three times, says the race distance is easy to understand and resonates with fans. And, coming on the back of Kerr’s world record, who can argue with him?

This is the first time the mile has been run at the games since 1966 and the hope is that tonight’s final matches the Miracle Mile run in 1954. Earlier that year Bannister broke the four-minute barrier, only for Australia’s John Landy to go lower with a time of 3:58.0 soon after. The Games in Vancouver were the first time two sub-four minuters had gone head-to-head. And the race didn’t disappoint – Bannister beating Landy with a time of 3:58.8 minutes. The Australian also ran under four minutes, making it the first time two men had done so in the same race.

Obviously all three of the expected main protagonists will go well under four minutes, but if they can recreate the drama of the 1954 final then we’ll have a race to savour.

Stay here for all the action with the gun set to go off at 8.55.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso welcomes Mykhailo Mudryk back to Chelsea after 4-year doping ban cut short but admits Blues future unclear
Sports.content:
XABI ALONSO is ready to welcome Mykhailo Mudryk with open arms after the end of his doping ban.

The Chelsea winger, 25, saw his four-year ban cut short this week after the FA and the World Anti-Doping Agency resolved their disciplinary process against him following an appeal.



Mudryk tested positive for a of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance, in 2024 and was slapped with a four year ban which he appealed with the Court of Arbitration for Sport this year.

The £62million forward has always maintained he never intentionally took the substance and changes to testing processes mean that, had the sample been taken today he would not have been reported as failing a drugs test.



Alonso, who had not expected to be working with Mudryk at Chelsea, confirmed the winger will join his squad for the next leg of their pre-season tour, in Hong Kong – despite the fact they have not spoken yet.

He said: “We are happy for him, especially for him, because probably we are not able to understand what he has been through in this time and how does he feel at the moment with the things that he had to cope with.



“We want that he feels part of a team, because he has been training on his own for a long time, and that we have the support from everyone, from the club, from the team-mates, from the staff, and for sure it will take time.

“Once he is with us, we will see how things develop.

“He is coming to Hong Kong, but I haven’t spoken to him yet.”

While many at Chelsea are excited to have Mudryk back, there is yet to be any clarity on his future at the club. He has a contract which runs for another five years, to 2031, but no decision has been made regarding his place in the squad for this season so far.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Alonso added: “We need to see, it’s too early to tell, to see how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of this game time that you need to be involved again, so it’s still early to tell.

“We were not expecting to have this great news at this moment, so we are very happy. We feel that he will be working with us.”

Chelsea ended the Australian leg of their tour with a late 2-1 defeat to London rivals Tottenham, who had ten men for almost the entire second half.

The Blues were without goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, who suffered a small knock.



Meanwhile, striker Joao Pedro is in talks over a new contract with the club, who are confident he will agree terms.

Pedro was a target for Barcelona at the start of the summer window, but Chelsea dubbed the Brazilian striker “untouchable” this summer and are pushing to tie him down further.

The forward only joined from Brighton last summer and the 24-year-old’s deal currently runs until 2033.

Sports.title: It’s a nice surprise to discover deep down football has a backbone.. but where’s this show of strength been hiding?
Sports.content:
WHAT a pleasant surprise to discover that­, buried deep, football actually does have a backbone.

It has been a delight to watch the sordid plan of suit-and-trainer wearing — creepy uncle at a wedding style — Gianni Infantino ­collapse around his own not-insignificant ears.



Uefa’s threat to boycott all but started the snowball.

Others attempted to look brave as they scrambled aboard the bandwagon which had been impressively assembled by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin.



But, sorry to complain at what is undoubtedly a triumph in the face of attempts to ­further b*****dise football, where has this sudden show of strength been when we needed it before?

Football has needed this newly-discovered might of its leaders and governing bodies time and time again.



Yet they have often been too cowardly or self-interested to stand up for supporters or those they represent.

Where were you when we needed to stop hydration breaks, half-time shows, Sunday night kick-offs or the omnipresence of that ‘Here we go’ touting wally on social media? It is true they are trivial points but all of them have got under the skin of fans at one point or another in recent years.

They are also a window to the serious problems which occur across the game, and all too often involve Fifa.

Belgium, Germany and Norway all publicly expressed their dismay over Fifa’s bowing to Donald Trump over Folarin Balogun’s one-match suspension for the United States’ round of 16 tie at the World Cup.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The decision to allow the striker to face Belgium was as dodgy as they come and they did not even try to hide that fact from us all.

As soon as the world learned that Infantino had taken calls from the US President — who just happened to have been the recipient of the first Fifa Peace Prize — a boycott would have been fitting.

It may seem extreme but Infantino’s spineless approach to Trump tainted his precious tournament.

What was the point of everyone else ­putting all that effort in if the hosts could fix any problems with a phone call to the man who is supposed to uphold and champion the rules?



Even though Belgium dismantled a Balogun-led USA 4-1 in the last-16, a united front at that moment — in the middle of a major tournament — would have made quite the statement, one Infantino and Fifa could not have stood up to.

Ticket prices, the barring of Sudanese referee Omar Artan from officiating at the tournament and the treatment of Iran were all largely greeted with a shrug from around the world.

Uefa quickly sailed in to appoint Artan to their Super Cup match between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa this month.

But that appeared to stem from a dislike of Infantino and a shot at a quick PR win rather than anything more moral.



A firm stance in Qatar at the World Cup four years ago would have been welcomed.

Instead the European nations’ show of support for human rights and the LGBTQ+ community fell down under the ­terrifying threat of a yellow card.

Those Fifa-approved armbands Harry Kane and his fellow captains ended up sporting in 2022 must have really warmed the hearts of the oppressed in the Middle East.

None of this is to say that Ceferin has not done well to gather the whole of Europe into what is undoubtedly a noble stand.



It would have been easy to swing the powerful nations behind a boycott but smaller federations tempted by Infantino’s promise of riches would have taken persuading.

This must set the tone for what Uefa has to stand for going forwards if it is to mean anything.

Let’s not forget this is a body which bowed to the Super League plotters by needlessly expanding the Champions League, dulling the experience for fans and piling more minutes into the legs of shattered stars.

Wake-up calls for those at the top are always helpful but did the collapse of the Super League really prevent Europe’s powerhouses from running the game? No.

Governing bodies must fight for football more often, otherwise their standing up to Fifa merely looks to be a move laced in self-interest by Uefa’s top man.



ED’S TOON’S BEST BET

A PAL in the pub recently lumped a few quid on Newcastle to get relegated at 40-1.

The fact he is a Sunderland fan may have tipped the scales but it is looking like a spot of superb foresight.

Just over a week on and that price has collapsed and may shorten further after the Toon effectively forced out their greatest asset in recent years.

Up against the expectations of a club the size of Newcastle, let alone their Saudi benefactors, Eddie Howe overdelivered given what he had to work with.

Chronic mismanagement and snail-paced decision-making made it an impossible task and, for his sake, it was wise to jump now.



Should his next club offer proper support, they will be very lucky indeed — as I would be if I listened to my mate’s tips more often.

RISEN FROM THE ASHES

THE drumbeat for Ben Stokes’ Ashes return appears to have started a little over a month after he retired.

All England fans want to see him in one last dust-up with the Aussies.

And given the narcissistic way he left the international stage, they may well get their wish — albeit not as captain.



Stokes will not be able to resist the storyline of riding back into the Test side next year to beat Australia.

FANS IN A MUD-DLE

CONFIRMATION that he is allowed to start playing football again will have been a delight to Mykhailo Mudryk after his doping ban.

The news was celebrated by some Chelsea supporters as if the Ukrainian would return like a new mega-money signing, a fresh star for Xabi Alonso to work with.

Have they forgotten just how hopeless the winger was at times?

Ten goals in 73 appearances does not scream superstar.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

I watched him play ten minutes of a charity match at Stamford Bridge — and he even struggled in that.

Those fans may soon recall why they were not too bothered by his suspension in the first place.

Sports.title: Arsenal in classy gesture after fans left fuming by £7 PPV for Girona pre-season friendly suffering technical glitch
Sports.content:
ARSENAL made their pre-season friendly against Girona FREE to watch after a technical issue stopped fans from streaming the scheduled pay-per-view offering.

The Gunners had advertised the fixture to buy for £6.99 prior to kick-off.



Supporters could also purchase a £14.99 bundle which gives them access to stream four pre-season fixtures.

However, many viewers missed the first half of the Girona match after being unable to log on to the club app or website.



Several fans took to social media to complain.

And at half-time, Arsenal responded by making the match free to view on YouTube.



A statement from the club read: “Arsenal supporters, apologies for the inconvenience. We’re working through some issues on Arsenal.com and The Arsenal App.

“Tonight’s game is now being streamed for free on our YouTube channel.”

The Gunners went on to win the match 4-1 against Girona.

Kai Havertz opened the scoring after latching onto a brilliant through ball from Max Dowman and slotting his shot into the bottom corner.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

New signing Christos Tzolis then scored a debut goal from the edge of the box to make it two.

Arnau Martinez got one back for the hosts just after the break, but Dowman restored the two-goal advantage moments later.

And Gabriel Jesus came off the bench to make it four.

Marli Salmon, Andre Harriman-Annous and Ceadach O’Neill were among the academy stars to appear on the night.

The Gunners next face Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday.

Sports.title: England wag Megan Pickford sparks fury with ‘offensive’ Princess Diana post as fans caught ‘off guard’ by comments
Sports.content:
ENGLAND World Cup Wag Megan Pickford has referenced Princess Diana in a TikTok about seatbelt safety.

Megan, 33, married to 32-year-old Three Lions and Everton goalie Jordan, was posting during her trip to Ibiza via private jet.



She captioned the video: “I love wearing my seatbelt in every environment.

If it can go wrong for Princess D it can go wrong for any of us.”



A comment said: “The Princess Diana bit caught me off guard.”

Diana died on August 31, 1997, after suffering fatal injuries in a car crash in the Pont de l’Alma road tunnel in Paris, France.



She was not wearing a seatbelt when she was travelling in the back seat of a chauffeur-driven Mercedes car with then boyfriend Dodi Fayed.

Mum-of-three Megan also said she had a crystal for “protection”.

She said: “I was not messing around for this trip, protection first.”

Megan’s holiday comes after England were defeated in the World Cup semi-finals in the US last month against Argentina.



She has been dubbed the ‘Queen of the Wags’.

She was seen promoting her designer outfits on social media during the tournament.

Sports.title: Newcastle fans already concerned as £23m summer signing is filmed training in shirt of Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
FOOTAGE has emerged of Newcastle new boy Sean Steur training in a Manchester United kit just days before his Toon transfer.

The Magpies shelled out £23million to sign teenage star Steur from Ajax in the wake of Sandro Tonali‘s £100m departure for Tottenham.



In a TikTok video posted by a Dutch performance centre just two days before Steur’s move was announced, the 18-year-old could be seen performing drills dressed head-to-toe in Man Utd training gear.

The clip has since been picked up on social media, with Red Devils fans teasing their Toon counterparts.



One wrote on X: “Already know who the real United are.”

And a second joked: “Boy doesnt like Zebra FC”.

Another added: “They should get him ready for us”.

Newcastle fans defended their new boy.

One blasted: “Worst attempt at s***housery ever”.

And a second insisted: “He joined the real UNITED”.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Others posted a snap of a young Michael Carrick wearing a replica Newcastle kit.

Steur gushed over his St James’ Park transfer after penning a five-year deal.

He said: “It’s an incredible feeling to be here. It’s a giant club in the Premier League and it was always my dream to play in the best league in the world, so this is really exciting.

“I was at home at Ajax – I joined when I was seven and I leave with only good memories, but when a club like Newcastle comes for you, it’s really hard to say no.



“The last few days have gone fast and I’m very happy to join.

“I’m a player who likes to get on the ball and play forward all the time. I’m happy playing between the lines and I feel I have a lot of energy in my game. I just want to win.”

Newcastle have lost the likes of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali already this summer, with Bruno Guimaraes nearing an Arsenal switch and Man Utd interested in Lewis Hall.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo set to marry Georgina Rodriguez in fairytale wedding on island where he grew up
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL star Cristiano Ronaldo is set to marry fiancée Georgina Rodriguez on the island where he was born and raised.

The pair appear to have decided to get hitched in Madeira.



The cathedral in the island’s capital Funchal is booked for a big wedding next Saturday, according to local reports.

Appropriately, weddings there kick off at 3pm.



Portugal star Ronaldo, 41 — who grew up in Funchal — and model Georgina, 32, are said to have reserved the nearby five-star Savoy Palace hotel for the reception.

A source said: “Guests at the hotel have been told two floors will be out of use on Friday and Saturday, as well as several bar areas.”



Ex-Manchester United forward Ronaldo now plays in Saudi Arabia.

He met Georgina, who is Spanish-Argentinian, in 2016 and proposed to her last August.

Last week the couple were snapped wearing diamond rings as they boarded a yacht in Majorca.

Ronaldo said previously that he and Georgina planned to marry after the World Cup, from which Portugal were ousted by eventual winners Spain last month.



The striker told Piers Morgan: “I hope to arrive at my wedding with the champion’s trophy.”

He said Georgina was the only woman he had dated that he had wanted to settle down with.

Sports.title: Music legend Phil Collins’ son Mathew, 21, joins former Bundesliga champions in shock transfer
Sports.content:
PHIL COLLINS’ son Mathew is looking to make his mark on the football world after completing a surprise transfer to former Bundesliga champions 1860 Munich.

The 21-year-old midfielder has signed a one-year contract with the German outfit after impressing during a trial spell.



Collins joins the club after spending last season with Austrian second-tier side Austria Salzburg.

The Switzerland-born youngster – whose half-sister is Lily Collins, of Emily In Paris fame – has spent the majority of his senior career in Austria after previously coming through youth systems in Germany.



And 1860 Munich confirmed the signing on Friday as they prepare for life in Germany’s fourth tier.

The historic club now compete in the Regionalliga after suffering relegation from the 3. Liga when they failed to secure the licence required to remain in the division.



Despite their current struggles, 1860 boast one of the richest histories in German football.

They were founder members of the Bundesliga in 1963 and famously won the German title during the 1965/66 campaign.

The club have also lifted the German Cup twice and reached the 1965 European Cup Winners’ Cup final, where they were beaten by West Ham at Wembley.

Collins began his career in the academies of Astoria Walldorf and Hannover 96 before moving to Austrian side WSG Tirol in 2023.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

During his time there, he even faced Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly, coming up against England captain Harry Kane in the summer of 2024.

Last season he made four league appearances for Austria Salzburg and also featured once in the Austrian Cup.

He linked up with his new team-mates ahead of their opening league match, a 2-2 draw away to FC Schweinfurt.

While Mathew is chasing his football dream, his famous father became one of the biggest names in music history.



Collins rose to fame as drummer and later lead singer of Genesis before launching a hugely successful solo career with hits including In the Air Tonight and You Can’t Hurry Love.

The music icon, who was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame both with Genesis and as a solo artist, has five children, including actress Lily, musician Simon Collins, actress and producer Joely Collins, and Mathew’s brother Nic.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Tzolis a livewire on Gunners debut as Dowman sparkles but Nwaneri off the pace in Girona win
Sports.content:
ARSENAL got their pre-season underway with a thumping win over Girona in the Catalan sunshine.

Mikel Arteta‘s side eased past their hosts, who were relegated from LaLiga last term.



The Gunners spent all week in Spain training ahead of this match.

And they looked sharp from the off, Kai Havertz firing them into the lead on 16 minutes and new boy Christos Tzolis doubling their advantage on the half hour.



Arnau Martinez pulled one back for the hosts, only for further efforts by Max Dowman and Gabriel Jesus to add gloss to the scoreline.

Here’s how SunSport’s Joshua Hall rated each Arsenal performer on a sweltering evening in Girona.

KEPA ARRIZABALAGA – 5

Had very little to do, but still couldn’t keep out Arnau Martinez’s second-half bullet header from a corner.

BEN WHITE – 6

Back from the injury that ruled him out of the Champions League final and the World Cup, and with the captain’s armband on.

A mixed performance that saw some sloppy touches, but also some great pressure to earn Arsenal their fourth goal with a tackle-cum-pass to Gabriel Jesus.

CRISTHIAN MOSQUERA – 6

Arsenal were not put under too much pressure by Girona, but Mosquera’s calm presence is always a comfort blanket when there is a wave of attack.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

PIERO HINCAPIE – 6

One of three World Cup stars to be given just over 30 minutes of action. Some nice link up play on the left flank when he was on the pitch.

RICCARDO CALAFIORI – 6

The Italian looked a threat when he was combining with Hincapie and Tzolis down the left side.

The game being played at a usual laid-back pre-season pace meant his usual marauding runs were out of the question.

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 7

Mikel Arteta looks like he views Lewis-Skelly as a midfielder now, starting him in that position from the off for this game.



A solid performance from the Englishman, but shifting into the middle of the park could still mean limited minutes if Bruno Guimaraes arrives.

KAI HAVERTZ – 8

A brilliantly taken opener from the German who still seems sharp from his time with Germany at the World Cup.

Whether or not the second goal was his is up for debate, the ball deflected off his ankle en route to the bottom corner from Christos Tzolis’ shot.



ETHAN NWANERI – 5

Arteta will be watching Nwaneri closely during pre-season, with his future at Arsenal still very much up in the air after his failed loan move to Marseille last term.

This was a solid enough performance with some nice close control, but the 19-year-old needs to have a more direct impact on the game.

MAX DOWMAN – 8

Not that anyone was doubting it, but Dowman’s raw talent is evident every time he gets the ball.

His through ball to find Havertz for the opener was sublime, and there were some moments of silky ball control scattered throughout his cameo too.

A brilliant solo goal topped off his performance, cutting in from the right flank and drilling the ball into the back of the net with his left peg.



CHRISTOS TZOLIS – 8

Some really promising stuff from the summer signing.

Tzolis was always looking to cut in on his right foot and get a shot off or find a man in the box, while he also offered a bit of set piece threat.

He will be claiming the second goal as his own after it was his goalward effort that deflected off Havertz and into the back of the net.



VIKTOR GYOKERES – 6

The Swede was given just 32 minutes after his World Cup exploits, but showed for the ball in his usual passionate manner for each and every one of them.

The final pass never really came.

SUBSTITUTES

FABIO VIEIRA – 4

Vieira is keen to leave Arsenal for Hamburg this summer after a successful loan in Germany last term.



This performance didn’t do much to make Arteta desperate to convince him to stay, in fact he was subbed off just over half an hour after coming on.

GABRIEL JESUS – 7

Did very well to tuck away the loose ball that fell into his path when Ben White forced an error at the back for Girona.

MARLI SALMON – 7

So assured on the ball for a centre-back of his age and comfortable under pressure too.

Arsenal fans will be hoping they will see more of the rising star this season, especially with William Saliba’s back injury.

ILLAN MESLIER – 7

Some really tidy saves from the new arrival, who joined on a free transfer after his Leeds contract expires this summer.



With so many youth players on the pitch alongside him, Meslier stepped in to clean up their mistakes.

REISS NELSON – 5

Another player who seems destined for the exit doors this summer. The winger had little impact during his cameo.

IFE IBRAHIM – 6

An exciting talent who loves to break up play and sit at the base of midfield. Like most of the youth talents brought on, it would have been nice to see him play alongside more first-team players.



BRAYDON CLARKE – 6

Son of former Premier League and Championship midfielder Nigel Quashie, Clarke was one of many youth players who held their own to maintain Arsenal’s cushion in the last 30 minutes.

ANDRE HARRIMAN-ANNOUS – 6

Always trying to make something happen, but didn’t quite get the opportunity to grab a goal given the gamestate when he was brought on.

CEADACH O’NEILL – N/A

ISMEAL KABIA – N/A

JOSH OGUNNAIKE – N/A

There was also some praise from United defender Leny Yoro. "He's a really good player," he said. "Still really young, still a lot to learn, a lot to improve. He's really humble, still working, so I'm happy for him to get his first minutes, so I hope for him it's going to continue like that."

‌



Yoro himself made his debut for Lille aged 16 and joined United for £52million, becoming the most expensive player under the age of 18 in the history of the game two years ago.

"I can see myself," Yoro added before offering some advice. "[I would say] stay humble, just want to work, and this is what we need in the team, even for the young guys.

"They're all doing really well, and JJ is one of them, so I hope he's going to learn a lot, continue like that, improve, yeah. But he's really good, a good player."

‌



View 2 Images JJ Gabriel came on to replace Bryan Mbeumo in the 82nd minute (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Gabriel trained with the first team last season and will hope that Carrick's presence as manager can aid his progression in the 2026/27 campaign. With some senior players yet to return following the World Cup, there has been a youthful look to the United team in pre-season, with Gabriel one of a number of academy players hoping to catch the eye.

Shea Lacey started and won the penalty which Mbeumo converted to make it 1-1, while Jack Fletcher - a half-time substitute for Amad - intercepted the ball and provided the assist for the Cameroon international's winner.

‌



Carrick was happy with what he saw from the mixture of young and experienced players. “The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company," he told MUTV.

"Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Sports.title: Max Dowman oozes class as new Arsenal partnership unlocked in Girona win – 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Max Dowman oozes class as new Arsenal partnership unlocked in Girona win – 5 talking points

GIRONA 1-4 ARSENAL: Max Dowman grabbed the headlines as Mikel Arteta's side put in a strong pre-season display against Spanish opposition

View 4 Images Max Dowman and Christos Tzolis were on target for Mikel Arteta's Arsenal against Girona

Arsenal strode to a 4-1 victory over Girona in their first official clash of pre-season with Max Dowman grabbing a goal and assist. Kai Havertz, Christos Tzolis and Gabriel Jesus were also on target with Ethan Nwaneri and Riccardo Calafiori making attacking contributions, but it was Dowman that stole the show.

‌



The opening goal arrived just after the quarter-of-an-mark as Havertz finished calmly after a brilliant piece of skill and pass from Dowman. A second arrived on the 30th minute when Arsenal broke through Girona's press courtesy of an excellent Ethan Nwaneri pass into Riccardo Calafiori.

‌



The Italian moved the ball out wide to Tzolis with the summer signing using his quick feet to gain a yard of space with his effort nestling in the far corner after a deflection. Girona did pull one back from a corner early into the second period with Arnau Martinez heading past Kepa Arrizabalaga.

‌



Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes READ MORE :

Arsenal star refused to go on pre-season tour to force through summer transfer READ MORE :

However, that deficit was at one for minutes as Dowman and Jesus both scored in the space of two minutes. The latter took advantage of an error to poke home while Dowman fired an effort into the corner with his left foot from just outside of the box.

Arteta brought on several fringe and academy players during the second half with goalmouth action minimal as the final whistle edged closer. Nonetheless, it was a very good workout for several Arsenal stars and a confident showing in front of goal.

Here, Mirror Football takes a look at the biggest talking points from the victory.

‌



Dowman's busy display

Max Dowman was more or less involved in every piece of good play by Arsenal in the opening 45 minutes.

It was his smart turn that opened up a huge gap in Girona's midfield for the first goal and his pass was perfectly weighted into Havertz with the German taking one touch before sliding home.

Midway through the first half, he showed his awareness at the other end by intercepting a pass inside the defensive third as Girona threatened. He went on a jinking run just before half-time before falling to the floor after being crowded out by Girona players in the penalty area, but the referee dismissed appeals for a spot-kick.

‌



It wasn't the best start to the half for Dowman with a poor decision made when he received the ball in the final third. Viktor Gyokeres was in acres of space on the other side of the pitch and the pass was on but he opted to dribble forward before losing possession which resulted in the Swede screaming at him for not passing.

View 4 Images Max Dowman scored a great goal as Arsenal beat Girona

Dowman later got on the score sheet himself as he drove an effort into the back of the net from 20 yards after another precise forward pass by Myles Lewis-Skelly. The 16-year-old was back defending immediately after that and made a crucial interception but just moments later needed to be bailed out by Kepa Arrizabalaga after a mishit back pass.

‌



He was brought off on the hour-mark with cameras capturing him deep in discussion with Arteta on the sidelines. While he is not the finished article, Dowman's quality was clearly on display and he looks set for a breakout season at Emirates Stadium.

New partnership unlocked

Due to the sheer amount of squad depth at his diposal, Arteta can choose to deploy certain players with others in order to develop partnerships. Based on the first 45 minutes in Spain, expect to see Christos Tzolis and Riccardo Calafiori linking up frequently.

The latter is an unorthodox full-back and will often find himself in central areas. That was the case for Arsenal's second goal as he drove into Girona's half after receiving a sharp forward pass from Nwaneri with Tzolis later picked out on the touchline.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Calafiori continued his run forward which occupied defenders and opened up space for the Greek international to cut inside and send an effort into the far corner, albeit via a deflection.

Defensive struggles

Arsenal were not at their defensive best in Girona with substitute goalkeeper Illian Meslier forced into a number of saves. It is worth noting those came after a number of alterations but even at full strength, the Gunners didn't look that solid.

‌



Early into the clash, Ben White was caught out and left chasing Girona players while there were a number of sloppy passes among their own backline.

Perhaps what would have angered Arteta most was conceding from a corner with Arnau Martinez jumping unmarked to head home. Riccardo Calafiori is arguably the only regular starter that was deployed from the off but Arteta's favoured back four is unlikely to be deployed early in the season.

William Saliba has a back injury and Jurrien Timber looks set to be managed carefully. Gabriel Magalhaes will also likely be monitored as he has played a lot of minutes in the last few years.

‌



Signing a defender is not the priority but it is clear why there have been links to a number of cental defenders.

Early substitutions

It was somewhat surprising to see Viktor Gyokeres, Kai Havertz and Piero Hincapie taken off after the first drinks break midway around the 30th minute.

View 4 Images Kai Havertz was one of three Arsenal stars to play just 30 minutes against Girona

‌



However, it makes perfect sense considering that trio all reached the World Cup last-32 and were therefore late arrivals to pre-season. Gabriel Martinelli and Magalhaes were eliminated in the following round and based on this, will likely be eased back into action.

Arteta has faced criticism for overplaying the likes of Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka but it looks as though he is being extra careful now especially after a number of key players struggled with fitness issues during the second half of the season.

Guimaraes transfer incentive

Regardless of the strong performance, the need to wrap up a deal for Bruno Guimaraes promptly was clear before the pre-season clash had even got underway.

‌



Arteta named a strong starting XI but, on paper, the balance in midfield was not the best. Lewis-Skelly, Havertz and Nwaneri are all talented footballers in their own right but the midfield dynamic did leave Arsenal open at times.

Arteta does not have too much choice, however, with Martin Odegaard, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino all still on holiday after the World Cup.

Brazil duo Gabriel Martinelli and Magalhaes have made their returns which means Bruno Guimaraes' minimum rest period is also due to be up. However, it seems as though he will be heading to Arsenal's training camp now as opposed to Newcastle's with an £80m deal agreed.

‌



View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes looks set to join Arsenal from Newcastle United

Arteta needed this signing wrapped up quickly - simply because Guimaraes will be required for the opening few weeks of the season and also to have plenty of training sessions under Arteta and with his new team-mates.

Considering that Christian Norgaard, who was sat among the substitutes in Girona, is set to join Everton, the Guimaraes to Arsenal deal is now expected to ramp up.

Article continues below

The Community Shield against Manchester City takes place in just over two weeks and Guimaraes ideally needs to be starting as the likes of Phil Foden, Rayan Cherki and Elliot Anderson present more of a threat than Girona.

Sports.title: Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes
Sports.content:
Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal are hoping to sign Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior, but that has not stopped them from working on another transfer

View 2 Images Arsenal want to sign Vinicius Junior (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

Arsenal are working to sign Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid but remain in the market for Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez. The Gunners are said to remain interested in the Argentina star despite being ready to make a mega-money move for his La Liga rival.

‌



Atleti ace Alvarez has long been linked to the Gunners, who were reportedly willing to offer Viktor Gyokeres in a player-plus-cash arrangement. Diego Simeone's side have been reluctant to sell their star, with the forward particularly interested in a move to Barcelona.

‌



Nevertheless, the prospect of an incredible summer double deal seeing Arsenal pluck Vinicius and Alvarez from the Spanish capital appears to be on the cards. Signing either would be a significant statement from the north London side ahead of their Premier League title defence.

‌



According to The Independent, Arsenal continue to pursue a deal for Alvarez. It has also been suggested Arsenal are confident about their chances of securing Vinicius.

Meanwhile, a transfer to bring Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal from Newcastle seems to be drawing closer, with his future potentially settled within the coming week.

Arsenal reach transfer agreement with medical to come next in major Bruno Guimaraes boost READ MORE :

New Newcastle boss makes Bruno Guimaraes stance clear amid Arsenal offer READ MORE :

The arrival of those players would see Mikel Arteta significantly improve his depth at the Emirates. The Spaniard would be able to choose a front three of Vinicius, Alvarez, Bukayo Saka, with the likes of Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke and new signing Christos Tzolis available for rotation.

‌



Arteta recently made it crystal clear he needed to strengthen his squad with additional elite players if they were to continue challenging across four competitions.

He said: "From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level. That is going to require a better squad, better individual.

"We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully, very soon, we can start to put things in a very concrete way."

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal are still working on a move for Julian Alvarez (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arteta continued: "This has to be the start and this has to be the standard. Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future.

‌



"The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition because we've shown that we've got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level. We want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.

"My ambition is that daily we nail the standards and the requirements to be better the following day. That is the thing that we have to control, and maintain that ambition, that discipline, that commitment and that positive energy through 11 months. That is the responsibility that we all have. If we all achieve that, we are going to be in a really strong position in May."

Sports.title: Chelsea squad's immediate reaction to Mykhailo Mudryk bombshell and imminent return
Sports.content:
Chelsea squad's immediate reaction to Mykhailo Mudryk bombshell and imminent return

Mykhailo Mudryk can officially return to football, and his Chelsea team-mates have made their feelings perfectly clear

View 2 Images Levi Colwill was one of many Chelsea stars to send a message to Mykhailo Mudryk (Image: (Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images))

Several Chelsea stars have issued messages of support to Mykhailo Mudryk after his doping ban was lifted. The 25-year-old has not played for the Blues since November 2024 after testing positive for meldonium and being handed a four-year suspension by the FA

‌



Earlier this week, a statement was released by English football's governing body which stated that that disciplinary proceedings against the Ukrainian had been resolved. A provisional ban was placed on Mudryk a month on from his failed test.

‌



During his time out, an appeal was lodged with the Court of Arbitration for Sport while confirmation of a hearing being set arrived in May of last year with 'written submissions' also exchanged. However, the situation has now been resolved with Mudryk posting on social media after the decision was made official.

‌



Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso gives Mykhailo Mudryk update as winger handed green light to return READ MORE :

His Chelsea team-mates Levi Colwill and Reece James led tributes by reposting his official statement to their Instagram stories. Romeo Lavia, Nicolas Jackson, Robert Sanchez, and Malo Gusto all followed their lead.

Meanwhile, former teammates including Ben Chilwell, Marc Cucurella, and Christopher Nkunku, alongside Cole Palmer, Enzo Fernandez, Moises Caicedo, Pedro Neto, and Wesley Fofana, were amongst the 1.5 million users to 'like' the Ukrainian's post.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Almost 60,000 users also flooded the comment section with messages of support. It is understood that Mudryk will now travel to Hong Kong to link up with the Chelsea squad ahead of Wednesday's friendly against Juventus.

Speaking to journalists at the Accor Stadium in Sydney, Australia, on Saturday, following a 2-1 defeat to Tottenham Hotspur, Alonso described the winger as a 'special' player, while tempering expectations regarding any immediate return to action.

"We are happy for him, especially for him," said the Blues manager. "Probably, we are not able to understand what he has been through in this time and how does he feel at the moment with the things that he had to cope with.

‌



"We want that he feels part of a team, because he has been training on his own for a long time, and that we have the support from everyone, from the club, from the teammates, from the staff, and for sure it will take time. So once he is with us, we will see how things develop."

On Mudryk's future, Alonso said: "We need to see, it's too early to tell, to see how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of this game time that you need to be involved again, so it's still early to tell."

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso's latest Chelsea press conference was dominated by Mykhailo Mudryk

‌



The Chelsea boss added: "We have the Mudryk that [we had], it will take time, but once there is a change, things start moving, and for him it's a massive change. So he trained on his own every day, and I think it had to be really, really hard, because he wanted to play football.

"He wanted to be part of a team, and he was not allowed to do that for such a long time. So once this big change has happened, now things will move on, and afterwards we will see if it's quicker, if it's slower, but we need to be aware of that."

Reflecting on Mudryk's abilities as a footballer, Alonso said: "Yeah, I remember watching him in Shakhtar, the impact he had, how quick he is, how good in one-on-one situations, how he could create a lot of situations on his own, and he's a special player, but he will take time for sure."

Article continues below

"To be honest, we were not expecting to have this great news at this moment, so we are very happy. We feel that he will be working with us."

Sports.title: West Ham break silence on ownership after Amanda Staveley’s consortium 'agrees 25% stake'
Sports.content:
West Ham break silence on ownership after Amanda Staveley’s consortium 'agrees 25% stake'

West Ham United have released a statement which throws the future of the club ownership into doubt, and leaves them in limbo until after the summer transfer window shuts

View 2 Images Amanda Staveley is reported to have agreed a deal for a 25 per cent stake in West Ham (Image: Anthony Devlin/Getty Images for IWG)

A consortium led by Amanda Staveley has agreed to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham United. Since news broke on Saturday afternoon, the Championship club have given an update in an official statement.

‌



The move comes after the family of the late David Gold agreed to sell 16 per cent of their stake to Royal Mail owner Daniel Kretinsky earlier this summer. It, however, has emerged that Staveley's consortium offered a higher price to buy the full Gold stake.

‌



Staveley’s intervention comes weeks after David Sullivan, 77, resigned as West Ham co-chairman in June after allegations of sexual abuse were reported by a Times and BBC Panorama investigation. Sullivan denies the allegations, calling them “factually incorrect and entirely false”.

‌



As things stand, Staveley or Kretinsky would still need to buy Sullivan's 38.8 per cent share to take majority control of the club.

In a club statement, released on Saturday evening, the Hammers said: "West Ham United can confirm it is aware of the announcement from Joint-Chair Vanessa Gold that she has reached a provisional agreement to sell her shares to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"The proposed transaction will now be subject to a pre-emption rights process. This provides all existing shareholders with the opportunity to acquire their proportional percentage of shares in round one, and any remaining shares in round two. This process will take approximately two months and, until it is completed, nothing will change regarding the ownership structure of the Club.

"West Ham United would like to assure supporters that the day-to-day running of the football club is in no way affected by this situation.

"Preparations for the new season continue to take shape with diligence and focus, and we thank all fans for their continued loyal backing at this time.

‌



"The Club will be making no further comment while the pre-emption process runs its course."

Staveley is known in English football for leading the Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund's takeover of Newcastle United. She left her role as a director at the club in 2024.

The consortium who have agreed a deal for the stake in West Ham is led by Staveley, alongside her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi and their firm PCP Capital Partners. They are said to be in partnership with the American private investment firm Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

‌



View 2 Images Amanda Staveley is the former co-owner of Newcastle United (Image: Lucy North/PA Wire)

Following the twist, a spokesperson for Krentinsky, who still owns 27 per cent of the club, told The Times: “The agreement we had reached with the Gold family in June provided stability for the club at a crucial time.

“This does the opposite. We will always act in the best interests of West Ham United and are reviewing all of our options, including exercising our pre-emption rights in full.”

‌



Meanwhile, representative of the Gold family, Vanessa Gold, said: “On the 12th of June Daniel Kretinsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

"In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family's shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led my Amanda Staeley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners. While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.

"My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League."

Article continues below

West Ham suffered relegation to the Championship at the end of last season. They start their bid for an immediate return on Sunday, August 15, when they travel to take on fellow relegation sufferers Burnley at Turf Moor.

As things stand, no new faces have been brought in by the club as yet in the transfer market. However, West Ham have done some strong business by collecting around £155m for Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville combined, and they have managed to keep Jarrod Bowen at the London Stadium.

Sports.title: Staveley-led consortium agrees deal for minority stake in West Ham
Sports.content:
Vanessa Gold has confirmed she has agreed to sell her stake in the club to a consortium led by former Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley.

Gold, who succeeded her father David as joint-chair of the Hammers following his death in 2023, has a deal in place with a group headed by Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners for her family's 25.1 per cent holding.

However, current shareholders will also be presented with the chance to buy out the Gold family under an ongoing process.

Image: Former Newcastle co-owner Staveley's consortium is set to buy a 25.1 per cent stake in the club

"Amanda Staveley, her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, PCP Capital Partners along with Ashland Forest Capital Partners can confirm they have agreed the purchase of the Gold family's 25.1 per cent stake in West Ham United," the Staveley-led consortium said in a statement.

"A legal binding agreement has been signed.

"This sale agreement, though, remains subject to a pre-emption process under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

"No further comment will be made whilst the ongoing legal process takes its course."

Sky Sports News further understands Staveley, Ghodoussi and their consortium have brought together considerable funds.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of West Ham's pre-season friendly against Stevenage

Gold said in a statement: "As the daughter of David Gold, it was a great honour to step into a joint-chair and director role at the club following his passing in 2023.

"Whether as a youth-team player, a lifelong fan or an owner, my father's priority was always to champion and protect this great club. Over the past three years I have taken huge personal pride in continuing that legacy and will always be hugely grateful to the staff, players and fans who allowed me to do so.

"On June 12, Daniel Kretinsky and I agreed a sale that would have made EP Group the single largest shareholder in West Ham. Unfortunately, since that time, the original deal and other alternatives that we have discussed could not be brought to fruition.

"In light of this, I have now reached an agreement to sell my family's shareholding to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners. This sale remains subject to a pre-emption process, under which existing shareholders have the option to buy the shares instead.

"While the process has not yet concluded, I wanted to be open with our fans about where things stand and my intentions.

"My ambition throughout this process has been to ensure the club has the right leadership and ownership to enable West Ham to achieve its potential and return to its rightful place in the Premier League.

Image: The consortium is led by Staveley and her husband Mehrdad Ghodoussi, alongside PCP Capital Partners

"Amanda Staveley, Mehrdad Ghodoussi and PCP Capital Partners will bring deep experience and understanding of what it takes to lead a successful football club, and I have every confidence in what she and her partners can bring to West Ham.

"While the sale process proceeds, I will continue to act in the club's best interests, as my father did and would expect of me."

Staveley brokered the deal which allowed a Saudi-backed consortium to buy out then Newcastle owner Mike Ashley in October 2021, and she and Ghodoussi oversaw the club's rise from Premier League relegation candidates to Champions League participants and, after their departure during the summer of 2024, Carabao Cup winners.

The Hammers dropped out of the top flight at the end of last season and will begin the process of attempting to secure a swift return at Burnley on August 16.

West Ham said in a statement: "West Ham United can confirm it is aware of the announcement from joint-chair Vanessa Gold that she has reached a provisional agreement to sell her shares to a consortium of PCP Capital Partners, led by Amanda Staveley and Mehrdad Ghodoussi, in partnership with Ashland Forest Capital Partners.

"The proposed transaction will now be subject to a pre-emption rights process. This provides all existing shareholders with the opportunity to acquire their proportional percentage of shares in round one, and any remaining shares in round two. This process will take approximately two months and, until it is completed, nothing will change regarding the ownership structure of the club.

"West Ham United would like to assure supporters that the day-to-day running of the football club is in no way affected by this situation. Preparations for the new season continue to take shape with diligence and focus, and we thank all fans for their continued loyal backing at this time.

"The club will be making no further comment while the pre-emption process runs its course."
