Sports.title: Evening Saigon wins Stewards' Cup at Goodwood
Sports.content:
James Doyle picked the right one from three choices as his bosses at Wathnan Racing topped an amazing week at Glorious Goodwood with victory in the Coral Stewards' Cup with Evening Saigon.

The win was a feather in the cap for the owners, who target this fixture with a vengeance, but perhaps more telling it was a second major handicap of the week for Qatari-born trainer Hamad Al Jehani.

Having also won the Golden Mile with Archivist when Doyle picked the wrong one, Al Jehani was able to celebrate a famous victory with the whole team on this occasion.

Despite higher numbers being preferred at Thursday's draw, the finish was dominated by the eventual winner drawn in 10 beating Stratusnine in five. Jamie Spencer flew from the back on Mitbaahy for third but he was beaten a head and a short head. Completely Random was fourth.

"It's been a great week. Obviously I was very deflated last year with just one and we were really frustrated by that so the memo was we need to do better and that's everyone, including me as well," said Doyle.

"We've done a lot of work this week looking at different tactics and things like that, track position and stuff. All the guys back home in the office, these guys, Hamad has done an unbelievable job with this horse as well.

"He's not an easy conveyance, setting off he was that well in himself he tried to get rid of me the first few strides but that was great.

"We just had the perfect set-up. Dark Thirty was near me, I was able to draft in behind him and we didn't go that mad I didn't think for a Stewards' Cup so I was happy to pull him out before the two and set sail for home.

"I knew the second horse, I won on him the other day at York, he's a pretty decent horse too so it was a good tussle up to the line.

"Hamad and his team, it's nice that they have won the two big handicaps this week."

Al Jehani said: "I am very happy for Evening Saigon and very happy for the team. He performed very well at Royal Ascot and it was the right decision from the management to keep him for the Stewards' Cup.

"It's really important for us and it's a really important race for the season. I'm very happy and thanks to James for giving the horse a great ride.

"It's not easy to be competitive with the best trainers in the world but we try our best and I think we are building in a very good way, with great help from the management. Hopefully, we will improve year by year and we can make Wathnan be in the winner's enclosure more and more."

Wathnan's racing advisor Richard Brown added: "James had a bit of a hard choice but he was pretty firm on riding this lad in the end. Hamad has turned up and won two of the hardest handicaps to win all year. We plot these and work as a team - when these results come off, it's just fantastic for Wathnan and what Wathnan is all about.

"If you look at Hamad's statistics since he started training, they match up with the best trainers in the country. He's a phenomenal horseman and was a very good rider himself. He's very modest about it but he showjumped to a good level. He's a great horseman and he's formed a great team. We all work very closely together and to pull this off is huge for everybody involved."

Goodie Two Shoes sticks her neck out to edge Lillie Langtry battle

Goodie Two Shoes needed to be very brave as she added to Joseph O'Brien and Dylan Browne McMonagle's fantastic week at Goodwood in the Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes.

With three winners already in the bag, the JP McManus-owned Goodie Two Shoes was sent off an 8/1 chance to bag a first victory of the season but looked to face a tough ask as Santorini Star kicked for home.

She still had ground to make up with 100 yards to the line but the seven-year-old stuck her neck out right where it mattered to get the verdict by a nose.

Image: Goodie Two Shoes (centre), ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle, on the way to winning the Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes at Goodwood

Goodie Two Shoes was second in the Melbourne Cup in November and a return to Australia will surely now be on the cards following this Group Two triumph.

The winning rider said: "She's a lovely filly, she's improving all the time since she started coming back this year, she's got better with each run.

"I was quietly confident she would get a lot closer to these fillies, she ran well last year [third] when the ground turned up soft but she would gallop down the road for you, she handles quick ground. I got a lovely split through them and she wanted to win.

"To be honest I didn't think I'd won but I looked back at the camera and she had her head stuck down for me at the right time; I did think Tom (Marquand) had won but we came out the right side of it.

"These are very, very special silks to put on. A big thanks to JP for putting me up and she's going to have a nice campaign through to the end of the season.

"I'm sure the Melbourne Cup is probably the main target, the boys will know that and Joseph and JP will discuss it but I'd probably guess that's the obvious target."

Sir Anthony McCoy, representing McManus, said: "I didn't think she had won but Jason Weaver said right on the nod, not before the line or after the line but right on the line, she put her head in the right place.

"She got a good ride - he was going to ride her for that bit of luck, down the inside, and he got a lot of luck. When you are as good as Dylan Browne McMonagle and you are riding for Joseph O'Brien, you seem to get a lot of luck.

"Dylan was over at mine a few times when he was 11 or 12. He is very mechanically correct, like Ryan Moore, and he's got that chip - that little thing where he could go the wrong way. I mean it in a good way. As Frankie found out one day at Ascot, he has that little edge to him.

"She was second in a Melbourne Cup and I thought she had been quite well handicapped for the Galway Plate if she ran there off 123. It's nice when you win races like this and hopefully she will be able to go back to the Melbourne Cup."

Sports.title: Warrington go fourth as Wakefield move second, Saints beaten by York
Sports.content:
Super League: Warrington move into fourth with comprehensive win over Castleford, St Helens beaten by York in thriller, and Wakefield regain second

Warrington got back to winning way on their visit to Castleford

Warrington Wolves moved up to fourth in the Betfred Super League table after recovering from a lacklustre start to claim a comprehensive 48-18 win at Castleford Tigers .

Having lost four of their last six matches, including three in a row on the road, Warrington were made to pay for an error-strewn first 20 minutes as the Tigers went 16-6 ahead at the OneBore Stadium.

But Matty Ashton, Toby King and Toafofoa Sipley touched down to turn the tide and put Warrington 24-18 in front at half-time, and James Harrison and Leon Hayes extended the Wolves' lead after the break.

Ashton scored again, taking his tally to five tries in two matches against Castleford this year having bagged a hat-trick when Warrington claimed a 72-6 victory in March, before Ben Currie scored.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Teenage scrum-half Ewan Irwin was excellent with the boot, splitting the posts with all eight conversions, to make it back-to-back defeats for Castleford.

While Castleford were stuffed by rivals Wakefield last weekend, they claimed a shock win over Leeds in their last home match and Warrington head coach Sam Burgess had warned they would be no pushovers.

On this occasion, they could not find the defensive intent required to stop Warrington on their push for a spot at the top end of the top six.

Sailor misses late kick as York edge thriller

Oli Field's double further dented St Helens' play-off hopes despite Jack Welsby's try-of-the-season contender as York edged to a thrilling 34-32 victory at the LNER Community Stadium.

Saints got off to the perfect start when Welsby kicked through to allow Jake Davies to touch down, with Jackson Hastings adding the conversion.

York Knights inflicted a damning loss on St Helens

York hit back almost immediately when Toa Mata'Afa put Jon Bennison over in the corner, and although he was unable to convert his own score, he was successful after Field capitalised on Cody Hunter's well-timed pass with a neat step to make it 10-6.

The lead proved short-lived when Hunter was unable to claim Hastings' up and under and Shane Wright pounced to score a converted try, and the visitors surged further head when Welsby burst through Denive Balmforth's tackle after the fleet-footed Harry Robertson had raced down the right wing.

However, Balmforth swiftly made amends with a sniping finish and Bennison levelled it up at 16-16 at the break.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The Knights were temporarily reduced to 12 when Ata Hingana was sent to the bin for a high tackle on Davies, but it was they who regained the lead with 53 minutes gone when prop Paul Vaughan barged his way over and Bennison added the extra points.

They went 12 points ahead after Saints failed to deal with Hunter's lofted kick, Nikau Williams touching down and Bennison making it 28-16, but Robertson's brilliance allowed Tristan Sailor to feed Welsby to complete a length-of-the-field move which was converted by Hastings.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Field's second try and a fifth successful Bennison conversion gave the Knights breathing space, but late scores from Robertson and Jacob Douglas gave Saints a chance.

Regular goal kicker Hastings remained on the field but was holding his glute so Sailor had to deputise and missed the crucial kick to level the game.

Wakefield move back second with win over Catalans

A crucial double from Isaiah Vagana helped Wakefield Trinity to a 32-12 win over Catalans Dragons to move back into second place in the Super League table.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The match was close at the break, Trinity leading by just four points, but a five-minute spell changed the game thanks to Vagana's quick efforts.

Jake Trueman and Cameron Scott had gone over early to give the visitors the lead before Catalans responded through Toby Sexton.

After Caleb Hamline-Uele and Matthieu Laguerre then put more points on the scoreboard for both outfits, Vagana's moment arrived with just 15 minutes remaining before Scott sealed the deal with his second.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The night was dampened further for Catalans with one minute remaining when Ugo Tison was sent to the sin bin for his hit on Jack Sinfield.

If Wakefield manage to hold onto second until the end of the season, it will be their best ever Super League finish.

Sports.title: Welbeck completes move to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Chelsea have completed the signing of Danny Welbeck from Brighton for an undisclosed fee.

Chelsea have turned to Welbeck as they look to add experience to manager Xabi Alonso's squad.

The last time the west London club paid a transfer fee for a player over the age of 26 was four years ago, when they signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from Barcelona.

Image: Welbeck is set for a medical ahead of a move to Chelsea

It has been two years since Chelsea selected a player over the age of 30 in any game.

Welbeck has continued to be a reliable goalscorer in the Premier League at 35. He scored 13 last season, and 10 during the campaign before that.

His arrival is another example of Chelsea prioritising physically-imposing players with Premier League experience this summer.

They have already signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117m - a record fee for a British player - and have brought in Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix.

It would also place further doubt on the futures of strikers Nicolas Jackson, Liam Delap and Marc Guiu.

Chelsea have signed several players from Brighton in recent seasons, including their main striker Joao Pedro, plus Moises Caicedo, Marc Cucurella and Robert Sanchez.

Several Brighton staff members have also moved to Stamford Bridge over the past four years, including sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Sam Jewell.

Welbeck reveals 'immense pride' at move

Welbeck says he already feels at home following "fantastic conversations" with Alonso and his relationships with some of the current Blues squad.

"When you hear of the interest from Chelsea, it's something that fills you with such immense pride," said Welbeck.

"Knowing the history of Chelsea, it's a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season.

"I'm really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time.

"I know a few of the boys already, and I've had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection.

"I've got that fire in my belly, and I'm ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.'

Neville backs Chelsea decision to sign PL experience

Gary Neville has said signing players like Welbeck and Jordan Henderson is exactly what Chelsea's young players need in order to gain more guidance.

The former Premier League-winning captain insists the decision to bring the veterans in is not a "magical" one, but rather an example of what all top teams need to compete.

"If you watched Chelsea for the last three, four or five years you'd say there's inexperience right throughout the football club," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Gary Neville says Chelsea have been crying out for Premier League experience in their squad, backing any decision to sign the likes of Welbeck and Henderson

"I think putting a spine in of good, senior professionals who act as guardians of good behaviour, responsibility and discipline in the dressing room is something that's not magic. It's something all top teams have had for many decades.

"Putting in Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck who know how to win Premier League titles, their jobs will be as much off the pitch as it will be on it. They're still good players who can contribute 25-35 games a season, but they will make sure the young players turn up every single day and give their all.

"I didn't think the young players at Chelsea have any real leadership or guidance on and off the pitch. They've now got people who can do that."

BlueCo's drastic change in transfer policy

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz explains why Chelsea's transfer policy U-turn - including potential signings Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson - makes sense.

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

The BlueCo era at Chelsea has been defined by hoarding some of the best young talent on the planet and developing them in-house. That method has had some successes, but overall, it has not panned out.

Image: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang was the last player over the age of 26 who Chelsea paid a transfer fee for

There is clearly some recognition and accountability from the top brass about that. In bringing in Alonso as manager, they know they have lucked out in getting one of the most sought-after tacticians in the game. The Spaniard has clearly identified the need for experience and the club are following his lead.

The interest in Granit Xhaka earlier in the summer was among the first signs of the shift. Even making a move for Lacroix is evidence of a change in approach.

The Welbeck move is surprising, but there is some logic that can be applied to it. Is he going to start every week? No. However, Chelsea's other four senior strikers have an average age of just 23. Combined, they have made 269 Premier League appearances and scored 74 goals.

Image: Thiago Silva was the last player over the age of 30 to play for Chelsea

The Brighton veteran has 400 appearances and 90 goals on his own. To have that as your back-up to the young guns you want to develop makes sense.

Henderson? That's a complete 180-degree turn. Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez are two of the more experienced players Alonso has. If you had to pick anywhere Chelsea needed a wise head, you would not say midfield.

Yet, they wanted Xhaka. They will soon have Henderson. Alonso may have been the man to oversee the blossoming of players like Florian Wirtz at Bayer Leverkusen. However, he clearly sees the values of opposite characters and knows Chelsea, and perhaps more importantly, he needs people ready now.

Sports.title: Riley leads by one shot ahead of final round of Rocket Classic
Sports.content:
Davis Riley shot a seven-under 63 to reach 15 under on Saturday and take a one-shot lead going into the final round at the Rocket Classic in Detroit.

Riley closed with consecutive birdies, making a 54-foot putt followed by a 10-footer to pull into a first-place tie with Michael Brennan.

Brennan had a strong round with seven birdies, but missed a nine-foot putt to bogey 18 and lost his share of the lead.

Rasmus Hojgaard, Chris Kirk, Rickie Fowler, and Cameron Young sit three shots back. Xander Schauffele is in a group another stroke back going into the final round on Sunday.

Sports.title: There can be no letup. Humiliated Infantino must stand down at Fifa or be removed | Nick Ames
Sports.content:
There is no time to dance around the subject. Gianni Infantino must stand down as Fifa president or otherwise be legally removed. No fresh chances can be made available for an official who has demolished trust in football’s integrity and governance, trashing all remaining credibility of the body that oversees the world’s most-cherished sport.

Infantino was forced into a humiliating climbdown on Saturday morning when he accepted the failure of his plan to sell off portions of the World Cup to private investment. He resolved to resume dialogue about football’s growth “in the spirit of shared interest in our game”. But such a naked attempt to save his own skin cannot hold. Every day Infantino remains in power is a fresh stain on an institution whose reputation is on the floor.

The overreach involved in unilaterally launching the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme – with its vision to place huge influence on football’s future in the palms of venture capitalists – would be enough to bring down most leaders. But Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond that. He has routinely made a mockery of Fifa’s own statutes and governance regulations, so nobody should be surprised that patience has finally snapped in corridors of power globally. Fifa’s “football unites the world” slogan has never looked more empty.

Article 10.3 of those regulations, which specifically pertains to the presidency, requires the incumbent to ensure “Fifa’s objectives, mission, strategic direction, policies and values are sustainably pursued, protected and implemented, and that a positive image of Fifa is fostered”. It stipulates “promoting friendly and peaceful relations within Fifa”, which is a nonsense given the degree to which federations and senior personnel have distanced themselves from Infantino in recent days.

The rules give no green light to the pursuit of multiple private projects that, most recently in lockstep with the current US administration or its tributaries, have been tabled with scant appetite for oversight or explanation.

Where to begin? The Folarin Balogun saga tipped many leading figures in football, particularly in Europe, towards the edge. There had already been widespread bafflement and disgust at Infantino’s presentation of the new Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump in December, with little background given about the process and highly contestable information provided about the US president’s qualifying achievements. Stakeholders were frustrated by a lack of consultation about the introduction of “hydration breaks”, which fundamentally toyed with the fabric of matches at this summer’s World Cup.

View image in fullscreen The saga involving Folarin Balogun after his ban for a red card was suspended tipped many leading figures in football towards the edge. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

The bizarre expedited bidding process for the 2034 tournament, which resulted in Saudi Arabia’s candidature being waved through in December 2024, also brought widespread criticism. This list only covers the past 20 months of controversies inflicted by Infantino, capped on Friday by revelations that plans for a 64-team World Cup are in full swing.

When a scathing statement from Uefa on Saturday called for an end to “secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game”, it was not only referring to the FFE project and its casual sidelining of other decision makers within Fifa.

A critical mass has been reached. Uefa took a decisive lead in following more than a year of harsh words with strong, united action in pledging to boycott future Fifa tournaments if Infantino did not withdraw his plan. It undoubtedly influenced the outcome and the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, secured an achievement that may define his own reign. But it will mean nothing if Infantino, who is understood to have deployed a major consultancy to smooth relations with federations in recent days, is given the oxygen to dangle fresh promises and turn heads back towards the status quo.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino’s rap sheet goes far beyond attempting to launch the Fifa Forward Enterprise unilaterally. Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPA

There is an acknowledgment within Uefa and beyond that the pace must not let up. Senior figures are adamant Infantino must not survive the current scandal. Some insiders feel a crucial next step will be for member associations, the overwhelming majority of whom had formally pledged their support for Infantino’s re-election next March, to recall those letters.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Doing so requires a request to Fifa but could, in sufficient numbers, be a de facto vote of no confidence in Infantino. Fifa had lobbied aggressively for those submissions but many FAs would now be red faced if their expression of fealty towards Infantino was more widely publicised.

Member associations have a duty not to shrink in staving off existential threats to their sport otherwise they, like Infantino, are doing it an egregious disservice. Backing away now would mean leaving the job half done at best.

Uefa have pledged to devise a new method for distributing Fifa’s wealth, delving into its multibillion cash reserves without “selling the family silver”. Behind the scenes it continues to work with other confederations in an effort to find credible candidates for Infantino’s replacement, with a view to running in the election should the Swiss hold on until then. The present crisis can be used to reshape football for the better but only if Infantino is not in situ to impose the final say.

The alternative is that Fifa, and by extension the game, continue lurching from one disaster to the next. It is no laughing matter when the public conversation around football centres on one man, his ego and brazen ventures.

In December Zvonimir Boban, a former sidekick to Infantino as Fifa’s deputy secretary general, told the Guardian that “the way is lost” after the peace prize award to Trump. Fifa will not find a route back until Infantino plays no further part in its operation.

Sports.title: Transfer news: Welbeck joins Chelsea, Brentford complete record Sangaré deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea have signed Brighton’s veteran striker Danny Welbeck in a deal worth a reported £5m. Welbeck has agreed a two-year contract and will link up with Xabi Alonso’s squad on their pre-season tour.

The 35-year-old’s move to Stamford Bridge is a break from Chelsea’s policy of signing younger players with the potential to be developed. It is the first time they have paid a transfer fee for a player over the age of 26 since they signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from Barcelona in 2022 when the striker was 33.

“When you hear of interest from Chelsea, it’s something that fills you with such immense pride. Knowing the history of Chelsea, it’s a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season,” Welbeck said.

“I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time. I know a few of the boys already and I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection. I’ve got that fire in my belly and I’m ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.”

Alonso was keen to add experience to his squad after last season’s disappointing 10th-place finish in the Premier League. He opted for Welbeck after the former Manchester United and Arsenal forward enjoyed a memorable campaign with Brighton.

Welbeck, who has 42 caps for England, scored 13 goals in 37 Premier League games last term after netting 10 times in 2024-25.

Welbeck’s arrival in west London will raise questions about the future of Chelsea striker Liam Delap, who signed from Ipswich last season, as well as fellow forwards Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

Welbeck is the latest player to move from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years after João Pedro, Moisés Caicedo, Robert Sánchez and Marc Cucurella, who joined Real Madrid earlier this summer.

Chelsea spent a British record £117m to sign the England forward Morgan Rogers, 24, from Aston Villa in July. They also secured the France defender Maxence Lacroix, 26, from Crystal Palace for £52m earlier this week and signed Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, 21, for £43m.

Brentford seal record Sangaré deal

Brentford have signed the Mali international Mamadou Sangaré from ⁠Lens for a club-record fee, reported to be £39m. Sangaré, 24, joins Brentford on a five-year contract, with ⁠the option to extend for another year.

“Mamadou ​is someone ‌that we’ve tracked ‌for quite some time. He’s been on ‌our radar and was a player we were really keen to bring in,” the Brentford head coach Keith Andrews said. “He’s a humble young man, but he’s equally as ⁠determined to succeed in his career. He ​fits ​everything we want from ​a Brentford player, on and ​off the ‌pitch.”
