Sports.title: "Phenomenal horseman" praised for role in brilliant Goodwood week for Wathnan Racing
Sports.content:
"Phenomenal horseman" praised for role in brilliant Goodwood week for Wathnan Racing

Hamad Al Jehani took two big Goodwood prizes with his thoroughbreds, the Coral-backed Golden Mile and Stewards Cup. The team's seven winners were Wild Blossom, Flora Of Bermuda, Exclusive Code, Archivist, Silver Lake, Hopewell Rock and Evening Saigon

View 2 Images Trainer Hamad Al Jehani (left) with several members of the Wathnan Racing team after Evening Saigon won the Coral Stewards' Cup (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

"Phenomenal horseman" Hamad Al Jehani was praised for his role in a big week for Wathnan Racing at the 2026 Qatar Goodwood Festival.

‌



The trainer sent out Evening Saigon to land the Coral Stewards Cup on Saturday, just a day after fellow 16-1 shot Archivist bagged another big handicap on Friday, the Golden Mile with the same sponsors.

‌



The pair were among seven winners for the owners over the five days, scooping just over £218,000 in prize money from their races alone.

‌



"Hamad has turned up and won two of the hardest handicaps to win all year," said Wathnan's racing advisor Richard Brown.

"We plot these and work as a team – when these results come off, it’s just fantastic for Wathnan and what we are all about.

Top jockey Jim Crowley retires at 48 after horror fall at York led to five operations READ MORE :

“If you look at Hamad’s statistics since he started training, they match up with the best trainers in the country. He’s a phenomenal horseman and was a very good rider himself. He’s very modest about it but he showjumped to a good level.

‌



"We all work very closely together and to pull this off is huge for everybody involved.”

Wild Blossom got the ball rolling in the Alice Keppell Conditions Stakes on Wednesday and Flora Of Bermuda, Exclusive Code, Silver Lake and Hopewell Rock also hit the target.

James Doyle picked Evening Saigon from the three Wathnan Racing had in contention in the Coral Stewards Cup and although the sprinter used plenty of energy before the start, he had enough left to see off Stratusnine on the far side.

‌



Mitbaahy was closing the pair down and took third in Saturday's feature, with Completely Random a close-up fourth under the meeting's leading rider Ryan Moore.

View 2 Images Evening Saigon (red cap) won the Coral Stewards Cup (Image: Getty Images)

"I am very happy for Evening Saigon and very happy for the team," said Hamad Al Jehani. "He performed very well at Royal Ascot and it was the right decision from the management to keep him for the Stewards’ Cup.

‌



“It’s really important for us and it’s a really important race for the season. I’m very happy and thanks to James for giving the horse a great ride.

“It’s not easy to be competitive with the best trainers in the world but we try our best and I think we are building in a very good way, with great help from the management. Hopefully, we will improve year by year and we can make Wathnan be in the winner’s enclosure more and more.”

Handlers Archie Watson, William Haggas, Andrew Balding, Karl Burke and George Boughey all saddled winners for the team across the week.

Article continues below

"Obviously I was very deflated last year (at the meeting) so the memo was we need to do better and that’s everyone, including me as well,” Evening Saigon's rider James Doyle said.

"He’s not an easy conveyance, setting off he was that well in himself he tried to get rid of me the first few strides but that was great."

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan's plea boosts brain disease campaign led by England legend Nobby Stiles' son
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan's plea boosts brain disease campaign led by England legend Nobby Stiles' son

EXCLUSIVE: Just before he died, Kevin Keegan spoke to Nobby Stiles' son, John, and encouraged him to push on with a campaign for a fund to be established to help with the cost of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy

View 4 Images Kevin Keegan, who played 63 times for England, sent John Stiles a message of support

Retired footballers face being struck down with a brain disease at epidemic levels, campaigners warn.

‌



John Stiles, 62, son of 1966 World Cup legend Nobby Stiles, is calling for a fund to help with the cost of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE) due to heading the ball.

‌



Kevin Keegan sent him a message just before the Newcastle legend’s tragic death from cancer, telling him: “Keep fighting, John." Former Leeds man Stiles said ex-England boss Keegan was one of the key voices highlighting CTE.

‌



The brain disease has claimed the lives not only of John’s dad but also other players, including Scotland legend Gordon McQueen, former England and West Brom striker Jeff Astle and Chris Nicholl, the ex-Aston Villa and Northern Ireland player.

Funeral director Robert Bush who hoarded bodies and gave wrong ashes jailed READ MORE :

Chelsea hit with £10m fine and suspended transfer ban after Roman Abramovich breaches READ MORE :

View 4 Images John Stiles with a photo of his late dad, the Man Utd and England great Nobby Stiles (Image: Mirrorpix)

A coroner ruled Nobby died as a result of repeatedly heading the ball, which he did around 136,000 times in his career.

‌



Even John’s grandson George, 12, is aware of CTE and apologised for heading the ball to stop a goal in a recent junior game. John, from Doncaster, South Yorkshire, warned the future impact on players could be unprecedented.

He said: "We need a proper fund like the one in America, which had $1.5billion; the £1million fund set up by the FA and PL (Premier League) is just a stunt. It’s an insult. At the moment, the families are funding the treatment of ex-pros, and the taxpayer is covering costs through the benefits system, which is wrong.

“There are at least 55,000 ex-footballers in England. Research suggests there could be 16,500 to 27,500 footballers withdementia. That is as scandal. The boom in the women’s game is a real concern for me."

‌



View 4 Images John Stiles with a photo of his late dad, the Man Utd and England great Nobby Stiles

Norbert “Nobby” Stiles died in 2020, aged 78. His family had to sell his medals to help pay for his care.

Born in Collyhurst, Manchester, in 1942, he made 395 appearances for United between 1960 and 1971 and earned 28 England caps.

‌



He played every minute during the legendary 1966 World Cup campaign, despite his own concerns that he was going to be dropped after the Argentina game.

View 4 Images John Stiles with his dad Nobby at a dinner alongside 1966 England star Martin Peters

An FA Spokesperson said: "While the link between heading in football and long-term brain health remains the subject of ongoing scientific and medical research, we have consistently been at the forefront of efforts to help improve the safety of our game.

Article continues below

"We have led the way in this area to proactively review and strengthen player welfare across every level of English football, working closely with our domestic and international stakeholders.

"We were the first governing body to introduce comprehensive heading guidelines across both professional and grassroots football, and we continue to review and enhance our game-wide concussion protocols in line with worldwide best practice.

"We have also invested in and actively supported multiple independent research projects, often resulting in groundbreaking and valuable insight, in order to gain a greater understanding of this complex area through objective, robust and thorough analysis."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick drops clear hint over three Man Utd transfers after Atletico Madrid win
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick drops clear hint over three Man Utd transfers after Atletico Madrid win

Manchester United beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in a pre-season friendly in Sweden on Saturday in a match which offered plenty of clues to the club's transfer plans

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's squad for the 2026/27 season isn't settled yet (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick offered a telling hint towards his plans for the summer transfer window through his starting line-up against Atletico Madrid on Saturday.

‌



United came from behind to beat the Spanish side 2-1 in Sweden thanks to two goals from Bryan Mbeumo. The Cameroon international scored from the penalty spot to make it 1-1 after Shea Lacey was fouled before bundling in a second from Jack Fletcher's low cross.

‌



There were plenty of encouraging signs for Carrick, who has also overseen a 5-0 win over Rosenborg and a 1-0 defeat by Wrexham so far in pre-season. Further friendlies are scheduled against Paris Saint-Germain, Leeds and AC Milan before United begin their 2026/27 campaign against newly-promoted Hull City on August 22.

‌



United have used the summer transfer window to recruit Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, while a handful of players have left already. But it's clear that there is still more work to do, and that the current squad on pre-season tour isn't the one Carrick wants to start the campaign with.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bryan Mbeumo inspires Man Utd win vs Atletico Madrid as transfer hint drops - 6 talking points READ MORE :

Man Utd forward set for shock Premier League transfer 'approach' with stance clear READ MORE :

There were two changes to the starting XI from the United boss, with Radek Vitek and Joshua Zirkzee dropping out for Tom Heaton and Amad. Zirkzee scored and assisted in the thrashing of Rosenborg, yet only got 17 minutes as a substitute against Atletico Madrid, with Carrick prioritising playing time for others.

‌



The Dutch striker is on the transfer list and United hope to find a buyer for a player who has managed just nine goals in 75 appearances since making a £36.5million move to Old Trafford two years ago. Juventus are reportedly interested in Zirkzee, whose future is currently up in the air.

Vitek's status in the squad is clear, with United signing Darlow on a free transfer to become Senne Lammens' back-up. The 22-year-old impressed on loan with Bristol City last season and has no shortage of suitors, although his £10m valuation is yet to be reached. United are keen to cash in and reinvest the cash elsewhere.

View 2 Images Altay Bayindir was not involved against Atletico Madrid (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, Altay Bayindir was not involved at all against Atleti, with Heaton, Vitek and youngster Dermot Mee the three goalkeepers chosen by Carrick. Bayindir conducted a training session prior the game in Stockholm before taking a seat behind the dugout to watch proceedings.

Manchester Evening News reports that Bayindir is keen to leave United this summer to find regular minutes and that Celta Vigo are keen to sign the Turkey international on a season-long loan deal, while a Turkish side could sign him permanently.

Bayindir has made just 17 appearances for United since joining for £4.3m in 2023. He played second fiddle to Andre Onana initially before Lammens' arrival last season made it clear he wouldn't get a chance as No.1.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua has nothing to prove and should think long and hard about carrying on
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua has nothing to prove and should think long and hard about carrying on

Our man Barry McGuigan runs the rule over Anthony Joshua following his unconvincing comeback win over Kristian Prenga before taking on Tyson Fury

View 2 Images AJ was knocked down twice in the first round (Image: Matchroom Boxing/Getty Images)

Saddened but not surprised was my reaction when Anthony Joshua sank to the canvas 20 seconds into the fight in Saudi Arabia.

‌



Yes he got to his feet and won in the second. The kind of power he carries is the last thing that leaves you. Punch resistance is another matter.

‌



Once that goes, it never comes back. It only ever gets worse. This is the stage Joshua is at. He is vulnerable and his opponents know it.

‌



Tyson Fury would have been watching those first-round knockdowns and rubbing his hands. Before the Kristian Prenga bout I had Joshua favourite against Fury. That dynamic has now shifted. Everything would have to go right for Joshua to win.

Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury winner offered world title shot READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua told exactly how he can beat Tyson Fury READ MORE :

This is a brutal business and if I were Joshua, I would be thinking hard about carrying on. I would not want to enter the ring knowing I was not at my best.

Joshua has nothing to prove to anybody. He has been a vibrant, positive presence in British boxing, won Olympic gold and the world heavyweight championship. And he certainly doesn’t need the money.

‌



However, I realise how difficult it would be for him to step down at this stage from a fight of such magnitude. It has been brewing for the best part of a decade and is important for the whole boxing economy.

Fury was far from convincing himself, labouring to victory 24 hours earlier in Thailand against a 46-year-old Mariusz Wach, who was annihilated by Moses Itauma. Wach just got tired in the end.

You would have worried for Fury prior to the Prenga shock. The truth is they are both fading rapidly.

‌



View 2 Images Anthony Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

Inactivity will not have helped Joshua, who had fought only once in 22 months and, of course, was involved in a tragic accident only last December, which took a huge emotional toll.

The only way Joshua prevails against Fury is to stand on him and back him up. If he lands early and big, it’s over, no matter how suspect his chin.

Article continues below

This is the dilemma. If you have to be aggressive to beat an opponent you are more likely to walk on to a counter. Fury is likely to keep his distance early, tee off his jab then look to send a right straight down the pipe.

Alternatively, having noted Joshua’s increased vulnerability, Fury could just go for it like he did in the second Deontay Wilder fight. Either way it’s not going the distance, that much is clear.

Sports.title: Man Utd forward set for shock Premier League transfer 'approach' with stance clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd forward set for shock Premier League transfer 'approach' with stance clear

Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley had two loan spells in League One last season and now the young star is reportedly attracting Premier League interest

View 2 Images Man Utd striker Ethan Wheatley is being linked with Everton (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Everton are reportedly preparing a transfer approach for Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley. However, it is understood that nothing is advanced at this stage.

‌



The 20-year-old ended last season on loan at League One side Bradford City after spending the first half of the campaign with Northampton Town. The Red Devils youngster made 12 appearances for the Bantams in 2025/26 as he sought more senior first-team football.

‌



However, he failed to score for the West Yorkshire club and did not feature in either of their League One play-off semi-final fixtures with Bolton Wanderers. It came after Wheatley became United's 250th academy graduate to feature for the first team, making his debut in a 4-2 win over Sheffield United in April 2024.

‌



Bryan Mbeumo inspires Man Utd win vs Atletico Madrid as transfer hint drops - 6 talking points READ MORE :

After impressing in the academy, he was one of several young stars who joined first-team training back in October 2024 as Erik ten Hag prepared his side for their upcoming Europa League clash against Fenerbahce.

And Premier League side Everton are now reportedly interested in a deal. Journalist Fabrizio Romano has claimed that the Toffees are preparing a formal proposal and are expected to make an official approach to United shortly.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Our sister paper, the Liverpool Echo, understands that Everton are interested in Wheatley, but a potential deal is still some way off. It is also understood that the move is initially directed towards the club's academy.

The young star has also been linked with German Bundesliga side Schalke 04 and Dutch club SC Cambuur, but is still on United's books as it stands.

View 2 Images Ethan Wheatley had two different loan spells last season (Image: Cat Goryn/Shutterstock)

‌



Wheatley is under contract at Old Trafford until 2028, therefore interested parties would have to fork out a fee to land him on a permanent basis.

Following his recall from Northampton in January last season, manager Kevin Nolan said Wheatley had made lots of progress during his spell at the club and shared his disappointment at the forward's departure.

Sports.title: Arsenal reach transfer agreement with medical to come next in major Bruno Guimaraes boost
Sports.content:
Arsenal reach transfer agreement with medical to come next in major Bruno Guimaraes boost

Arsenal are hoping to sign Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes this summer, with a possible hint at their confidence in a deal

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is looking to stregthen his Arsenal squad ahead of the new season. (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal have reached an agreement to sell midfielder Christian Norgaard to Everton, in a hint over their confidence in completing a deal for Bruno Guimaraes. The Brazilian is a key transfer target for Arsenal this summer.

‌



As reported by the Liverpool ECHO, Arsenal have agreed a fee in the region of £7million with Everton over the sale of Norgaard. A medical is due to take place next week, ahead of the move being finalised.

‌



Norgaard only joined Arsenal last summer, but found game time hard to come by at the Emirates Stadium. Last season saw him make just seven appearances in the Premier League, with a further 18 coming in all other competitions.

‌



New Newcastle boss makes Bruno Guimaraes stance clear amid Arsenal offer READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Despite the lack of game time, selling the midfielder indicates that Arsenal expect more additions in the position, with Guimaraes emerging as a priority addition. Arsenal's interest in the Newcastle midfielder comes at a time of chaos at St James' Park.

It was confirmed this week that Eddie Howe has left his position as Newcastle boss. It was reported that his decision to leave the club was partly due to the possibility of Guimaraes being sold this summer, following the sales of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali.

‌



Incoming boss Matthias Jaissle is expected to hold face-to-face talks with Guimaraes. The chat will see him try to sell his vision and philosophy.

View 3 Images Arsenal are closing in on a transfer for Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire.)

However, it is expected that the two clubs will reach an agreement over a fee in the coming days. The transfer fee is expected to be at least £80million, possibly up to £85million with add-ons.

‌



If an exit for Norgaard, and a transfer for Guimaraes is sealed, then the Brazilian will add to Mikel Arteta's midfield options. Martin Odegaard is club captain and is joined by Martin Zubimendi, Declan Rice and Mikel Merino, with three of the four players still on their extended break following their success in the World Cup.

The talk over Norgaard's future comes after he made a promise last October. Speaking to Danish outlet Bold, he said: "I can guarantee that Arsenal will be my last club abroad.

View 3 Images Christian Norgaard is leaving Arsenal for Everton

‌



“I still want to return to Brondby when my contract at Arsenal expires. My contract is two years with an option for a further year.

“I would be happy to stay at Arsenal for the extra year if things develop in that direction. If it turns out that it wasn’t the right match, we’ll go home to Denmark after two years.”

Sports.title: England legend Peter Reid says FIFA chief Gianni Infantino must go 'for the good of the game'
Sports.content:
England legend Peter Reid says FIFA chief Gianni Infantino must go 'for the good of the game'

EXCLUSIVE: Gianni Infantino backtracked on his investment plan, which was rejected by three continental confederations, with UEFA having warned its nations would boycott FIFA events if it went ahead

View 6 Images Peter Reid, pictured at Wembley in 2022, has blasted the FIFA boss (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

England legend Peter Reid has slammed FIFA President Gianni Infantino and called for him to resign for the good of the game.

‌



His demand came as FIFA ditched plans to sell off part of the World Cup to private investors following a furious backlash. European football’s governing body UEFA condemned the “shabby, back room” deal and declared a loss of confidence in Infantino as pressure mounted on the beleaguered boss.

‌



Asked if Infantino should go, Reid, who played 159 times for Everton told the Sunday Mirror: “I cannot believe you are asking that question - it is like asking if the sky is blue when the sun is out."

‌



Gianni Infantino is so delusional he does not know his time is well and truly up READ MORE :

View 6 Images UEFA condemned the deal and says it lost confidence in Gianni Infantino (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

UEFA said: "UEFA welcomes FIFA’s decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions – including the World Cup – into private hands. The proposal was unanimously rejected by UEFA’s national associations and by many other federations and confederations of all sizes around the world, whose job it is to protect football.

‌



"UEFA thanks all the fans, leagues, clubs, players, individuals, associations and confederations that opposed the scheme, alongside the many Prime Ministers, Heads of State and commentators who have demonstrated to the FIFA President that football is not for sale."

They were backed by the FA who said: “We fully support UEFA’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

PM Andy Burnham, who previously said Infantino was the wrong man to lead the organisation, stressed her felt it was the right decision for FIFA to back down.

‌



View 6 Images Peter Reid and Diego Maradona at the 1986 World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Reid, who also played for Bolton Wanderers and manchester-city-fc>Manchester City, continued: "He must go - look at the World Cup: the hydration breaks for advertising, the half time show in the final. The rules of the game state it should be 15 minutes and it took more than half an hour.

“Do I think he should go? Yes. Private investors in football - that is just wrong. FIFA has hundreds of millions already, they should be putting more money into grassroots. That is where the money should go, instead of getting into bed with private investors.”

‌



Reid played for England in the infamous ‘Hand of God’ game, the 2-1 quarter-final defeat to Maradona's Argentina at the 1986 World Cup in Mexico, and represented his country 13 times.

View 6 Images Peter Reid greets PM Andy Burnham in Downing Street (Image: Dinendra Haria/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

He continued: “Infantino's position is untenable now, people have lost faith in him. You look at his private investment plan and its links to Donald Trump, it is just crazy. UEFA has come out against it and so has the Asian FA.

‌



“And I back them 100 percent, though don't forget that UEFA tried to launch the European Super League. FIFA should go back to the basics, concentrate on the game and the fans. The World Cup in America was just too expensive for ordinary people.

“I knew many fans who did go and they all said the same thing. It cost too much, and there was too much travelling. That was Infantino’s doing.”

Former Sunderland manager Peter turned 70 at the end of last month and is raising money for the Sir Bobby Robson Foundation. He added: “It’s an honour to still be part of his team 40 years after Mexico 86.”

‌



View 6 Images The England team at 1986 World Cup ahead of match against Argentina (Image: Mirrorpix)

The scathing statement from UEFA also said: “We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

“It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again.

‌



“That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

“When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA’s Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, ‘Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA’, before telling the assembled stakeholders, ‘The money of FIFA is your money. It’s not the money of the FIFA President. It’s your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else’."

View 6 Images Spain lift the World Cup last month (Image: Walid Ibrahim/JNA via ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

‌



It continued: “On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent. And with reserves standing at over $5bn, he has also failed to use associations’ money for the benefit of the game.

“UEFA will begin work immediately with partners and stakeholders all over the world and right across the game to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing FIFA Forward programme.

“We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in FIFA’s bank account to deliver the kick start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of FIFA. But we don’t need to sell off the family silver to pay for it.

Article continues below

“This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.

Prince Ali Al Hussein, who previously ran to be head of FIFA, called for an end to secret ballots to elect the organisation’s president.

He posted online: “With all the controversy surrounding FIFA, world football is facing a clear cut crisis in leadership just before an upcoming election. As someone who has been through this process before, I believe one thing needs to be done immediately: remove a secret ballot for Presidential elections! Every other decision including hosting the World Cup is now done openly, except -of course- for presidential elections..”

Sports.title: UEFA 'accelerating' efforts to force Gianni Infantino out of FIFA after embarrassing U-turn
Sports.content:
UEFA 'accelerating' efforts to force Gianni Infantino out of FIFA after embarrassing U-turn

Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president is looking more and more uncertain after he was forced to drop his plan to sell stakes in tournaments following a backlash led by UEFA

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino could be ousted as FIFA president (Image: Harry Murphy/UEFA via Getty Images)

UEFA have been emboldened by Gianni Infantino's humiliating U-turn on his controversial World Cup plans and are reportedly working hard to oust him from his position.

‌



Infantino's attempts to force through plans, in which stakes of tournaments like the World Cup would be sold to private investors, has fallen flat on its face. European football's governing body UEFA, CONCACAF, which represents North and Central America, and the Asian Football Confederation spoke out against the idea, killing it dead.

‌



Just days after announcing the plans, Infantino was forced to concede that it had "created divisions" and was "no longer in the interest" of the game. Having originally been conceived as a way of solidifying his support ahead of seeking re-election for a fourth term as FIFA president, the plans could now prove to be his downfall.

‌



UEFA have led the backlash against Infantino and are now considering the best way to remove him as FIFA president. Sky News reports that moves are 'accelerating' and there is 'a determined effort' to oust him. The report states that it is now not a question of if, but when, Infantino will be toppled.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

UEFA declare loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino in bombshell new statement READ MORE :

The easiest outcome would be to force Infantino to resign from a position he's held for 10 years. If not, they would need 43 of FIFA's 211 associations to ask for an emergency congress in order to hold a vote of no confidence in Infantino's leadership.

‌



Another option would be to rally support behind a rival in the upcoming election. TalkSPORT says UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has asked federations who have previously endorsed Infantino for a fourth term to revoke their letters. CONCACAF leader Victor Montagliani, or Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi, could be put forward to run against Infantino.

Whatever option they pursue, it is clear that UEFA is determined to use the current momentum to force lasting change at FIFA.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is facing mounting opposition (Image: PA)

‌



UEFA said in a statement on Saturday: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again.

"That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA’s confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

‌



"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA’s Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,' before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It’s not the money of the FIFA President. It’s your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent. And with reserves standing at over $5bn, he has also failed to use associations’ money for the benefit of the game.

‌



"UEFA will begin work immediately with partners and stakeholders all over the world and right across the game to propose a new way of distributing resources through the existing FIFA Forward programme.

"We must start to use some of that money that is sat idle in FIFA’s bank account to deliver the kick start that the grassroots and the wider game need in each of the 211 countries of FIFA. But we don’t need to sell off the family silver to pay for it.

"This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
